sentences.zh: =漢紀五十九=起閼逢敦牂，盡柔兆涒灘，凡三年。

translations.literal: [Han Records 59] Beginning with Yanfeng Dunxiang, ending with Rouzhao Toushan, three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Han Records 59] Spanning from the year Yanfeng Dunxiang through Rouzhao Toushan—a period of three years.

sentences.zh: 孝獻皇帝壬建安十九年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xian of Han [ren], Jian'an year nineteen (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xian of Han, nineteenth year of Jian'an (

sentences.zh: 甲午，公元二一四年）

translations.literal: jiawu, AD 214)
translations.idiomatic: jiawu, the year 214 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，馬超從張魯求兵，北取涼州，魯遣超還圍祁山。

translations.literal: Spring, Ma Chao asked Zhang Lu for troops, to take Liangzhou in the north; Lu sent Ma Chao back to besiege Qishan.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, Ma Chao asked Zhang Lu for troops to march north and seize Liangzhou; Lu sent him back instead to besiege Qishan.

sentences.zh: 姜敘等告急於夏侯淵，諸將議欲須魏公操節度。

translations.literal: Jiang Xu and others reported urgency to Xiahou Yuan; the generals discussed wanting to await orders from Duke Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xu and others sent urgent appeals to Xiahou Yuan; the generals debated whether they ought to wait for orders from Duke Cao.

sentences.zh: 淵曰：「公在鄴，反覆四千里，比報，敘等必敗，非救急也。

translations.literal: Yuan said: "The Duke is at Ye—a round trip of four thousand li; by the time word arrives, Xu and the others will surely have been defeated. That is not how to relieve an emergency."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said, "The Duke is at Ye, four thousand li there and back. By the time a report reaches him, Xu and the others will already have been defeated—that is no way to save them in time."

sentences.zh: 」遂行，使張郃督步騎五千為前軍。

translations.literal: " He then set out, making Zhang He command five thousand infantry and cavalry as the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: " He set out at once, placing Zhang He in command of five thousand foot and horse as the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 超敗走。

translations.literal: Ma Chao was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 韓遂在顯親，淵欲襲取之，遂走。

translations.literal: Han Sui was at Xianqin; Yuan wanted to strike and capture him; Sui fled.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui was at Xianqin; Yuan meant to take him by surprise, but Sui fled.

sentences.zh: 淵追至略陽城，去遂三十餘里，諸將欲攻之，或言當攻興國氐。

translations.literal: Yuan pursued to Lueyang city, thirty-odd li from Sui; the generals wanted to attack him, but some said they should attack the Xingguo Di instead.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan pursued as far as Lueyang, still thirty-odd li behind Sui. The generals wanted to press the attack on him, but others argued they should strike the Di of Xingguo instead.

sentences.zh: 淵以為：「遂兵精，興國城固，攻不可卒拔，不如襲長離諸羌。

translations.literal: Yuan thought: "Sui's troops are elite; Xingguo's walls are strong—an attack cannot be taken quickly. Better to strike the Changli Di."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan reasoned, "Sui's troops are first-rate, and Xingguo is strongly fortified—we cannot storm it in a hurry. Better to strike the Di of Changli."

sentences.zh: 長離諸羌多在遂軍，必歸救其家。

translations.literal: Most of the Changli Di were in Sui's army; they would surely return to rescue their families.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the Changli Di were serving in Sui's army; they would surely hurry home to defend their families.

sentences.zh: 若捨羌獨守則孤，救長離則官兵得與野戰，必可虜也。

translations.literal: If they abandoned the Di and held alone they would be isolated; if they rescued Changli the army could meet the enemy in the field and surely capture them.
translations.idiomatic: If they left the Di and held their ground alone, they would be isolated; if they rushed to save Changli, our troops could meet them in the open and take them for certain.

sentences.zh: 」淵乃留督將守輜重，自將輕兵到長離，攻燒羌屯，遂果救長離。

translations.literal: " Yuan then left supervising officers to guard the baggage train, personally led light troops to Changli, attacked and burned the Di encampments; Sui indeed came to rescue Changli.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan left supervising officers to guard the baggage train, led light troops himself to Changli, and attacked and burned the Di camps. Sui did come to the rescue of Changli.

sentences.zh: 諸將見遂兵眾，欲結營作塹乃與戰。

translations.literal: The generals saw Sui's troops were numerous and wanted to encamp and dig trenches before fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how numerous Sui's forces were, the generals wanted to entrench and dig trenches before giving battle.

sentences.zh: 淵曰：「我轉斗千里，今復作營塹，則士眾罷敝，不可復用。

translations.literal: Yuan said: "We have fought in relay for a thousand li; if we now make camps and trenches the troops will be weary and cannot be used again."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said, "We have fought our way a thousand li in relays. If we stop now to build camps and trenches, the men will be exhausted and good for nothing."

sentences.zh: 賊雖眾，易與耳。

translations.literal: Though the bandits are many, they are easy to deal with."
translations.idiomatic: The enemy may be many, but they will be easy to handle."

sentences.zh: 」乃鼓之，大破遂軍。

translations.literal: " He then beat the drums and greatly defeated Sui's army.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the drums beaten and routed Sui's army completely.

sentences.zh: 進圍興國。

translations.literal: He advanced to besiege Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to besiege Xingguo.

sentences.zh: 氐王千萬奔馬超，餘眾悉降。

translations.literal: The Di king Qianwan fled to Ma Chao; the rest all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Di king Qianwan fled to Ma Chao, while the remainder surrendered outright.

sentences.zh: 轉擊高平、屠各，皆破之。

translations.literal: He turned to attack Gaoping and the Tuge, breaking both.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned against Gaoping and the Tuge and defeated them both.

sentences.zh: 三月，詔魏公操位在諸侯王上，改授金璽、赤紱、遠遊冠。

translations.literal: Third month, an edict placed Duke Cao's rank above feudal lords and kings, changing to grant him the golden seal, crimson sash, and distant-travel crown.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, an edict ranked Duke Cao above all feudal lords and kings and invested him anew with the golden seal, crimson sash, and distant-travel crown.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，旱。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, during the fourth month, there was drought.

sentences.zh: 五月，雨水。

translations.literal: Fifth month, flooding rains.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month came heavy rains and flooding.

sentences.zh: 初，魏公操遣廬江太守朱光屯皖，大開稻田。

translations.literal: Initially, Duke Cao sent Lujiang Administrator Zhu Guang to garrison Wan, opening up large rice fields.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Duke Cao had sent Lujiang Administrator Zhu Guang to garrison Wan and open extensive rice paddies there.

sentences.zh: 呂蒙言於孫權曰：「皖田肥美，若一收孰，彼眾必增，宜早除之。

translations.literal: Lü Meng said to Sun Quan: "Wan's fields are fertile and rich; if they harvest once, the enemy's numbers will surely increase—we should eliminate them early."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng told Sun Quan, "Wan's fields are rich and fertile. One harvest there will swell their numbers—we should destroy this threat at once."

sentences.zh: 」閏月，權親攻皖城。

translations.literal: " In the intercalary month, Quan personally attacked Wancheng.
translations.idiomatic: " In the intercalary month, Quan led the assault on Wancheng in person.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲作土山，添攻具，呂蒙曰：「治攻具及土山，必歷日乃成；

translations.literal: The generals wanted to build earthen hills and add siege equipment; Lü Meng said: "Making siege equipment and earthen hills will surely take many days to complete;"
translations.idiomatic: The generals proposed building assault mounds and siege engines. Lü Meng said, "Siege works and earthen mounds cannot be finished in less than many days;"

sentences.zh: 城備既修，外救必至，不可圖也。

translations.literal: once the city's defenses are repaired, outside relief will surely arrive—we cannot achieve our aim.
translations.idiomatic: by then the defenses will be ready and outside relief will arrive—we will have lost our chance.

sentences.zh: 且吾乘雨水以入，若留經日，水必向盡，還道艱難，蒙竊危之。

translations.literal: Moreover we are entering on floodwaters; if we stay many days the water will surely subside, and the return route will be difficult—I privately deem this dangerous.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, we entered on the floodwaters. If we linger for days, the water will fall and the retreat will be hard—I fear that danger myself.

sentences.zh: 今觀此城，不能甚固，以三軍銳氣，四面並攻，不移時可拔；

translations.literal: Now observing this city, it is not very solid; with the three armies' sharp spirit attacking on four sides at once, it can be taken in no time;
translations.idiomatic: This city is not strongly built. Strike on four sides with the army's full edge, and it will fall in no time;

sentences.zh: 及水以歸，全勝之道也。

translations.literal: returning with the water is the way to complete victory."
translations.idiomatic: withdraw while the waters still hold—that is the path to total victory."

sentences.zh: 」權從之。

translations.literal: " Quan followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " Quan agreed.

sentences.zh: 蒙薦甘寧為升城督，寧手持練，身緣城，為士卒先；

translations.literal: Meng recommended Gan Ning as assault commander; Ning held a white silk rope, climbed the wall himself, leading the soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: Meng recommended Gan Ning to lead the escalade. Ning took a white silk rope, scaled the wall himself, and went first among the troops;

sentences.zh: 蒙以精銳繼之，手執枹鼓，士卒皆騰踴。

translations.literal: Meng followed with elite troops, beating drums; the soldiers all leaped upward.
translations.idiomatic: Meng followed with picked troops, beating the war drums, and the men surged up after them.

sentences.zh: 侵晨進攻，食時破之，獲朱光及男女數萬口。

translations.literal: They attacked at dawn and broke it by mealtime, capturing Zhu Guang and tens of thousands of men and women.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked at dawn and took the city by breakfast time, capturing Zhu Guang and tens of thousands of people.

sentences.zh: 既而張遼至夾石，聞城已拔，乃退。

translations.literal: Zhang Liao then arrived at Jiashi, heard the city was already taken, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao reached Jiashi only to learn the city had already fallen, and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 權拜呂蒙為廬江太守，還屯尋陽。

translations.literal: Quan appointed Lü Meng Lujiang Administrator and returned to garrison at Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Quan appointed Lü Meng Administrator of Lujiang and returned to camp at Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮留關羽守荊州，與張飛、趙雲將兵溯流克巴東。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang left Guan Yu to guard Jingzhou, and with Zhang Fei and Zhao Yun led troops upstream to conquer Badong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang left Guan Yu to hold Jingzhou and, with Zhang Fei and Zhao Yun, led troops upriver to take Badong.

sentences.zh: 至江州，破巴郡太守嚴顏，生獲之。

translations.literal: At Jiangzhou they defeated Ba commandery Administrator Yan Yan and captured him alive.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangzhou they defeated Yan Yan, Administrator of Ba commandery, and took him alive.

sentences.zh: 飛呵顏曰：「大軍既至，何以不降，而敢拒戰！

translations.literal: Fei shouted at Yan: "The great army has arrived—why do you not surrender but dare resist!"
translations.idiomatic: Fei thundered at Yan, "The main army is here—why do you not surrender? How dare you resist!"

sentences.zh: 」顏曰：「卿等無狀，侵奪我州，我州但有斷頭將軍，無降將軍也！

translations.literal: " Yan said: "You and your ilk are lawless, seizing our province—our province has only generals who lose their heads, no surrendering generals!"
translations.idiomatic: " Yan replied, "You people are shameless invaders of our province. In this province we have only generals who lose their heads—never generals who surrender!"

sentences.zh: 」飛怒，令左右牽去斫頭。

translations.literal: " Fei was enraged and ordered attendants to drag him off and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: " Fei flew into a rage and ordered his men to drag Yan away and behead him.

sentences.zh: 顏容止不變，曰：「斫頭便斫頭，何為怒邪！

translations.literal: Yan's bearing did not change; he said: "Behead if you will behead—why be angry about it!"
translations.idiomatic: Yan's composure never wavered. He said, "Behead me if you like—why work yourself into a rage over it?"

sentences.zh: 」飛壯而釋之，引為賓客。

translations.literal: " Fei admired him and released him, taking him as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: " Fei was impressed, released him, and took him on as a personal guest.

sentences.zh: 分遣趙雲從外水定江陽、犍為，飛定巴西、德陽。

translations.literal: They dispatched Zhao Yun by the outer water to secure Jiangyang and Jianwei; Fei secured Brazil and Deyang.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Zhao Yun along the outer river to secure Jiangyang and Jianwei, while Fei pacified Brazil and Deyang.

sentences.zh: 劉備圍雒城且一年，龐統為流矢所中，卒。

translations.literal: Liu Bei had besieged Luocheng for nearly a year; Pang Tong was struck by a stray arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei had besieged Luocheng for nearly a year when Pang Tong was hit by a stray arrow and died.

sentences.zh: 法正箋與劉璋，為陳形勢強弱，且曰：「左將軍從舉兵以來，舊心依依，實無薄意。

translations.literal: Fa Zheng wrote a letter to Liu Zhang, describing the strength and weakness of the situation, and said: "General Left from the time he raised troops has cherished his old ties—he truly has no shallow intent."
translations.idiomatic: Fa Zheng wrote Liu Zhang a letter laying out the balance of forces and adding, "From the day he raised his army, General Left has kept his old affection for you—he truly bears you no ill will."

sentences.zh: 愚以為可圖變化，以保尊門。

translations.literal: I deem that change can be contemplated to preserve your honored house."
translations.idiomatic: I believe you should consider a change of course to preserve your house and rank."

sentences.zh: 」璋不答。

translations.literal: " Zhang did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang made no reply.

sentences.zh: 雒城潰，備進圍成都。

translations.literal: Luocheng fell; Bei advanced to besiege Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Luocheng fell, and Bei pressed on to besiege Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮、張飛、趙雲引兵來會。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang, Zhang Fei, and Zhao Yun led troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang, Zhang Fei, and Zhao Yun marched up with their forces to join him.

sentences.zh: 馬超知張魯不足與計事，又魯將楊昂等數害其能，超內懷於邑。

translations.literal: Ma Chao knew Zhang Lu was not worth plotting with; moreover Lu's officers Yang Ang and others repeatedly harmed his abilities—within, Chao was anxious.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao saw that Zhang Lu was no partner for serious plans, and that Lu's officers such as Yang Ang kept undermining him; inwardly he grew restless.

sentences.zh: 備使建寧督郵李恢往說之，超遂從武都逃入氐中，密書請降於備。

translations.literal: Bei sent Jianning Supervisor Li Hui to persuade him; Chao fled from Wudu into the Di territory and secretly wrote requesting surrender to Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Bei sent Li Hui, Supervisor of Jianning, to win him over. Ma Chao fled from Wudu into Di country and sent a secret letter offering to surrender to Bei.

sentences.zh: 使人止超，而潛以兵資之。

translations.literal: Bei had someone hold Chao back while secretly supplying him with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Bei had men hold Ma Chao in place while secretly reinforcing him with troops.

sentences.zh: 超到，令引軍屯城北，城中震怖。

translations.literal: When Chao arrived, he was ordered to lead troops camped north of the city; the city was shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Chao arrived, Bei had him camp north of the city with his army, and panic seized Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 備圍城數十日，使從事中郎涿郡簡雍入說劉璋。

translations.literal: Bei besieged the city for some tens of days and sent Attendant of the Masters of Writing Jian Yong of Zhuo commandery to persuade Liu Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: After besieging the city for several tens of days, Bei sent Jian Yong of Zhuo, Attendant of the Masters of Writing, into the city to persuade Liu Zhang.

sentences.zh: 時城中尚有精兵三萬人，穀帛支一年，吏民咸欲死戰。

translations.literal: At that time the city still had thirty thousand elite troops, grain and cloth enough for a year; officials and commoners all wanted to fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: The city still held thirty thousand crack troops and provisions for a year; officials and commoners alike were ready to fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 璋言：「父子在州二十餘年，無恩德以加百姓。

translations.literal: Zhang said: "Father and son have been in this province more than twenty years without conferring grace on the common people."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang said, "Father and son have ruled this province for more than twenty years without bestowing any real grace on the people."

sentences.zh: 百姓攻戰三年，肌膏草野者，以璋故也，何心能安！

translations.literal: For three years the common people have fought; their flesh and fat nourishing the wild grass—for Zhang's sake—how can my heart be at ease!"
translations.idiomatic: For three years the people have fought, their flesh feeding the wild grass—all because of me. How could my conscience bear that!"

sentences.zh: 」遂開城，與簡雍同輿出降，群下莫不流涕。

translations.literal: " He then opened the gates and rode out in the same carriage with Jian Yong to surrender; all below wept.
translations.idiomatic: " He opened the gates, rode out in the same carriage with Jian Yong to surrender, and every man under him wept.

sentences.zh: 備遷璋於公安，盡歸其財物，佩振威將軍印綬。

translations.literal: Bei moved Zhang to Gong'an, returning all his valuables, granting him the seal and sash of General Who Inspires Awe.
translations.idiomatic: Bei resettled Zhang at Gong'an, returned all his property, and invested him with the seal and sash of General Who Inspires Awe.

sentences.zh: 備入成都，置酒，大饗士卒。

translations.literal: Bei entered Chengdu, set out wine, and greatly feasted the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Bei entered Chengdu, set out wine, and gave the troops a great feast.

sentences.zh: 取蜀城中金銀，分賜將士，還其穀帛。

translations.literal: He took gold and silver from the Shu city, distributed them to officers and soldiers, and returned their grain and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: He took the gold and silver in the Shu capital, distributed it among the officers and men, and returned the people's grain and cloth to them.

sentences.zh: 備領益州牧，以軍師中郎將諸葛亮為軍師將軍，益州太守南郡董和為掌軍中郎將，並置左將軍府事，偏將軍馬超為平西將軍，軍議校尉法正為蜀郡太守、揚武將軍，裨將軍南陽黃忠為討虜將軍，從事中郎麋竺為安漢將軍，簡雍為昭德將軍，北海孫乾為秉忠將軍，廣漢長黃權為偏將軍，汝南許靖為左將軍長史，龐羲為司馬，李嚴為犍為太守，費觀為巴郡太守，山陽伊籍為從事中郎，零陵劉巴為西曹掾，廣漢彭羕為益州治中從事。

translations.literal: Bei took office as Governor of Yizhou, appointed Military Adviser Middle Gentlemen Zhuge Liang as General of the Military Advisers, Yizhou Administrator Dong He of Nan commandery as Supervisor of the Army Middle Gentlemen, jointly handling Left General headquarters affairs; General of the Van Ma Chao as General Who Pacifies the West; Military Adviser Colonel Fa Zheng as Shu commandery Administrator and General Who Displays Martiality; General of the Rear Huang Zhong of Nanyang as General Who Attacks the Barbarians; Attendant of the Masters of Writing Mi Zhu as General Who Pacifies Han; Jian Yong as General Who Displays Virtue; Sun Qian of Beihai as General Who Upholds Loyalty; Magistrate of Guanghan Huang Quan as General of the Van; Xu Jing of Runan as Chief Clerk to the Left General; Pang Xi as Major; Li Yan as Administrator of Jianwei; Fei Guan as Administrator of Ba; Yi Ji of Shanyang as Attendant of the Masters of Writing; Liu Ba of Lingling as Western Bureau Clerk; Peng Yi of Guanghan as Supervisor of the Masters of Writing for Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bei assumed the post of Governor of Yizhou. He made Zhuge Liang, Military Adviser Middle Gentleman, General of the Military Advisers; Dong He of Nan, Yizhou Administrator, Supervisor of the Army Middle Gentleman, sharing Left General headquarters duties; Ma Chao, General of the Van, General Who Pacifies the West; Fa Zheng, Military Adviser Colonel, Administrator of Shu and General Who Displays Martiality; Huang Zhong of Nanyang, General of the Rear, General Who Attacks the Barbarians; Mi Zhu, Attendant of the Masters of Writing, General Who Pacifies Han; Jian Yong, General Who Displays Virtue; Sun Qian of Beihai, General Who Upholds Loyalty; Huang Quan, Magistrate of Guanghan, General of the Van; Xu Jing of Runan, Chief Clerk to the Left General; Pang Xi, Major; Li Yan, Administrator of Jianwei; Fei Guan, Administrator of Ba; Yi Ji of Shanyang, Attendant of the Masters of Writing; Liu Ba of Lingling, Western Bureau Clerk; and Peng Yi of Guanghan, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing for Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，董和在郡，清儉公直，為民夷所愛信，蜀中推為循吏，故備舉而用之。

translations.literal: At first Dong He in the commandery was pure, frugal, and upright, loved and trusted by Han and Yi; Shu praised him as an orderly official, so Bei employed him.
translations.idiomatic: Dong He had earlier served in the commandery with purity, thrift, and integrity, winning the trust of both Han and tribal peoples; Shu hailed him as a model official, which is why Bei raised him up.

sentences.zh: 備之自新野奔江南也，荊楚群士從之如雲，而劉巴獨北詣魏公操。

translations.literal: When Bei fled from Xinye to the south of the Yangzi, Jing-Chu gentlemen followed like clouds, but Liu Ba alone went north to Duke Cao.
translations.idiomatic: When Bei fled from Xinye south of the Yangzi, Jing-Chu scholars flocked to him like clouds—yet Liu Ba alone went north to Duke Cao.

sentences.zh: 操闢為掾，遣招納長沙、零陵，桂陽。

translations.literal: Cao appointed him as a clerk and sent him to recruit Changsha, Lingling, and Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao took him on as a clerk and sent him to win over Changsha, Lingling, and Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 會備略有三郡，巴事不成，欲由交州道還京師。

translations.literal: When Bei had taken roughly three commanderies, Ba's mission failed; he wanted to return to the capital by way of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: But Bei had already seized some three commanderies, Ba's mission came to nothing, and he meant to return to the capital by way of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 時諸葛亮在臨蒸，以書招之，巴不從，備深以為恨。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang was then at Linzheng and wrote to recruit him; Ba would not come—Bei deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang was at Linzheng and wrote inviting him, but Ba refused; Bei took this as a deep affront.

sentences.zh: 巴遂自交趾入蜀依劉璋。

translations.literal: Ba then entered Shu from Jiaozhi to rely on Liu Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Ba then entered Shu from Jiaozhi and placed himself under Liu Zhang.

sentences.zh: 及璋迎備，巴諫曰：「備，雄人也，入必為害。

translations.literal: When Zhang welcomed Bei, Ba remonstrated: "Bei is a formidable man; if he enters he will surely do harm."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang welcomed Bei in, Ba warned, "Bei is a formidable man. Let him in and he will surely bring harm."

sentences.zh: 」既入，巴復諫曰：「若使備討張魯，是放虎於山林也。

translations.literal: " After Bei entered, Ba remonstrated again: "If you send Bei to attack Zhang Lu, it is releasing a tiger into the mountain forest."
translations.idiomatic: " Once Bei was inside, Ba warned again, "Send him against Zhang Lu and you are releasing a tiger into the hills."

sentences.zh: 」璋不聽，巴閉門稱疾。

translations.literal: " Zhang did not listen; Ba shut his door claiming illness.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang would not listen, and Ba shut his doors, pleading illness.

sentences.zh: 備攻成都，令軍中曰：「有害巴者，誅及三族。

translations.literal: When Bei attacked Chengdu, he ordered through the army: "Whoever harms Ba—execution extending to three clans."
translations.idiomatic: When Bei besieged Chengdu, he proclaimed through the army, "Whoever harms Liu Ba will bring execution on three generations of his kin."

sentences.zh: 」及得巴，甚喜。

translations.literal: " When he got Ba he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " When he secured Ba, he was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 是時益州郡縣皆望風景附，獨黃權閉城堅守，須璋稽服，乃降。

translations.literal: At that time the counties of Yizhou all submitted at the wind's sight; only Huang Quan shut the city and held firm, waiting until Zhang formally surrendered before he submitted.
translations.idiomatic: By then the counties of Yizhou were surrendering at the first rumor of Bei; only Huang Quan shut his gates and held out until Zhang had formally submitted, and then he yielded.

sentences.zh: 於是董和、黃權、李嚴等，本璋之所授用也；

translations.literal: Thus Dong He, Huang Quan, Li Yan, and others had been those Zhang employed;
translations.idiomatic: Dong He, Huang Quan, Li Yan, and others had been Zhang's own appointees;

sentences.zh: 吳懿、費觀等，璋之婚親也；

translations.literal: Wu Yi, Fei Guan, and others were Zhang's affinal kin;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yi, Fei Guan, and others were tied to Zhang by marriage;

sentences.zh: 彭羕，璋之所擯棄也；

translations.literal: Peng Yi was one Zhang had cast aside;
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yi was a man Zhang had cast out;

sentences.zh: 劉巴，宿昔之所忌恨也；

translations.literal: Liu Ba was one he had long resented;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ba was a man Bei had long resented;

sentences.zh: 備皆處之顯任，盡其器能，有志之士，無不競勸，益州之民，是以大和。

translations.literal: Bei placed them all in prominent posts, employing their full abilities; men of ambition all strove to encourage one another, and the people of Yizhou were thereby greatly harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Bei gave them all high office and used their talents to the full. Men of ambition strove to serve him, and the people of Yizhou were brought into broad harmony.

sentences.zh: 初，劉璋以許靖為蜀郡太守。

translations.literal: At first Liu Zhang had appointed Xu Jing as Shu commandery Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liu Zhang had made Xu Jing Administrator of Shu commandery.

sentences.zh: 成都將潰，靖謀逾城降備，備以此薄靖，不用也。

translations.literal: When Chengdu was about to fall, Jing plotted to flee over the wall to surrender to Bei; Bei for this held Jing in low regard and did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: As Chengdu was about to fall, Jing plotted to slip over the wall and surrender to Bei; for this Bei held him in contempt and would not use him.

sentences.zh: 法正曰：「天下有獲虛譽而無其實者，許靖是也。

translations.literal: Fa Zheng said: "Under heaven there are those who gain empty reputation without reality—Xu Jing is such."
translations.idiomatic: Fa Zheng said, "The world has men who win empty fame without substance—Xu Jing is one of them."

sentences.zh: 然今主公始創大業，天下之人，不可戶說，宜加敬重，以慰遠近之望。

translations.literal: Yet now the lord is founding a great enterprise—the people under heaven cannot be told household by household; he should receive added respect to comfort the hopes of near and far."
translations.idiomatic: Yet you are only now founding a great enterprise. You cannot explain yourself door to door across the realm; you should honor him publicly to satisfy the hopes of men near and far."

sentences.zh: 」備乃禮而用之。

translations.literal: " Bei then honored and employed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Bei thereupon treated him with ceremony and gave him office.

sentences.zh: 成都之圍也，備與士眾約：「若事定，府庫百物，孤無預焉。

translations.literal: During the siege of Chengdu, Bei made a pact with officers and soldiers: "When the affair is settled, treasury goods of a hundred kinds—I have no share."
translations.idiomatic: During the siege of Chengdu, Bei pledged to his officers and men, "When this is settled, everything in the treasury is yours—I claim no part of it."

sentences.zh: 」及拔成都，士眾皆捨干戈赴諸藏，競取寶物。

translations.literal: " When Chengdu was taken, soldiers all cast aside weapons and rushed to the storehouses, competing to take treasures.
translations.idiomatic: " When Chengdu fell, the men cast aside their arms and rushed to the storehouses, scrambling for valuables.

sentences.zh: 軍用不足，備甚憂之，劉巴曰：「此易耳。

translations.literal: Military funds were insufficient; Bei was deeply worried; Liu Ba said: "This is easy."
translations.idiomatic: Military funds ran short, and Bei was deeply troubled. Liu Ba said, "That is easily remedied."

sentences.zh: 但當鑄直百錢，平諸物價，令吏為官市。

translations.literal: Only need to cast zhibai cash coins, equalize prices of goods, and have officials conduct government markets."
translations.idiomatic: Mint zhibai coins, stabilize prices, and have officials run government markets."

sentences.zh: 」備從之。

translations.literal: " Bei followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " Bei followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 數月之間，府庫充實。

translations.literal: Within several months the treasury was full.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months the treasury was full again.

sentences.zh: 時議者欲以成都名田宅分賜諸將。

translations.literal: At that time debaters wanted to use famous Chengdu fields and residences to reward the generals.
translations.idiomatic: At the time some argued that the finest fields and houses in Chengdu should be divided among the generals as rewards.

sentences.zh: 趙雲曰：「霍去病以匈奴未滅，無用家為。

translations.literal: Zhao Yun said: "Huo Qubing, because the Xiongnu were not yet destroyed, had no use for a home."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yun said, "Huo Qubing refused to settle down while the Xiongnu still stood unconquered."

sentences.zh: 今國賊非但匈奴，未可求安也。

translations.literal: Now the national enemy is more than the Xiongnu alone—we cannot yet seek comfort.
translations.idiomatic: Our country's enemy is far more than the Xiongnu alone—we are in no position to seek comfort yet.

sentences.zh: 須天下都定，各反桑梓，歸耕本土，乃其宜耳。

translations.literal: We must wait until all under heaven is settled, each returning to native district, returning to plow native soil—that is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the realm is wholly pacified should each man return to his native place and take up farming at home—that is the proper course.

sentences.zh: 益州人民，初罹兵革，田宅皆可歸還，令安居復業，然後可役調，得其歡心，不宜奪之以私所愛也。

translations.literal: The people of Yizhou have newly suffered war; fields and residences can all be returned, letting them settle and resume work—then they can be levied and their goodwill gained; they should not be seized for private favorites."
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yizhou have only just suffered war. Their fields and homes should be returned so they can settle and resume their livelihoods—only then can you levy and win them. They must not be stripped to reward private favorites."

sentences.zh: 」備從之。

translations.literal: " Bei followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " Bei accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 備之襲劉璋也，留中郎將南郡霍峻守葭萌城。

translations.literal: When Bei attacked Liu Zhang, he left Central Regiment General Huo Jun of Nan commandery to guard Jimeng city.
translations.idiomatic: When Bei moved against Liu Zhang, he left Huo Jun of Nan, Central Regiment General, to hold Jimeng.

sentences.zh: 張魯遣楊昂誘峻求共守城。

translations.literal: Zhang Lu sent Yang Ang to entice Jun, asking to hold the city jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu sent Yang Ang to win Jun over and propose a joint defense of the city.

sentences.zh: 峻曰：「小人頭可得，城不可得！

translations.literal: Jun said: "This petty man's head can be taken, but the city cannot!"
translations.idiomatic: Jun replied, "You may have my head, but you will never have this city!"

sentences.zh: 」昂乃退。

translations.literal: " Ang then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Ang withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後璋將扶禁、向存等帥萬餘人由閬水上，攻圍峻，且一年。

translations.literal: Later Zhang's generals Fu Jin, Xiang Cun, and others led more than ten thousand men up the Lang River, attacked and besieged Jun, for nearly a year.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang's generals Fu Jin and Xiang Cun led more than ten thousand men up the Lang River to besiege Jun for nearly a year.

sentences.zh: 峻城中兵才數百人，伺其怠隙，選精銳出擊，大破之，斬存。

translations.literal: Jun had only several hundred soldiers in the city; watching for their slack moments, he chose elite troops to strike out, greatly defeated them, and beheaded Cun.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had only a few hundred men in the city. When he saw his chance, he sent picked troops out in a sortie, routed the enemy, and killed Xiang Cun.

sentences.zh: 備既定蜀，乃分廣漢為梓潼郡，以峻為梓潼太守。

translations.literal: After Bei had settled Shu, he divided Guanghan into Zitong commandery and made Jun Zitong Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Once Bei had secured Shu, he carved Zitong commandery out of Guanghan and made Jun its administrator.

sentences.zh: 法正外統都畿，內為謀主，一飧之德、睚眥之怨，無不報復，擅殺毀傷己者數人。

translations.literal: Fa Zheng outwardly governed the capital region, inwardly served as chief strategist; a meal's kindness or an eyelash's grudge—none went unavenged; he on his own authority killed several who had injured or insulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Fa Zheng governed the capital region outwardly while serving as Bei's chief strategist within. The smallest kindness or the slightest grudge he repaid in full, and he killed several men on his own authority who had wronged him.

sentences.zh: 或謂諸葛亮曰：「法正太縱橫，將軍宜啟主公，抑其威福。

translations.literal: Someone told Zhuge Liang: "Fa Zheng is too unbridled; the General should inform the lord and curb his power and privilege."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Zhuge Liang, "Fa Zheng runs wild. You ought to tell the lord to rein in his power."

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「主公之在公安也，北畏曹操之強，東憚孫權之逼，近則懼孫夫人生變於肘腋。

translations.literal: " Liang said: "When the lord was at Gong'an, he feared Cao Cao's strength in the north, dreaded Sun Quan's pressure in the east, and nearby feared trouble from Lady Sun at his elbow."
translations.idiomatic: " Liang said, "When our lord was at Gong'an, he feared Cao Cao's strength to the north and Sun Quan's pressure to the east, and close at hand he dreaded trouble from Lady Sun under his own roof."

sentences.zh: 法孝直為之輔翼，令翻然翱翔，不可複製。

translations.literal: Fa Xiaozhi aided him as wings, letting him soar aloft in a turn—this cannot be duplicated.
translations.idiomatic: Fa Xiaozhi was the wing that let him rise and soar again—an achievement that cannot be matched.

sentences.zh: 如何禁止孝直，使不得少行其意邪！

translations.literal: How can we restrain Xiaozhi and keep him from acting even slightly as he wishes!"
translations.idiomatic: How then can we restrain Xiaozhi and keep him from having his way even a little?"

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮佐備治蜀，頗尚嚴峻，人多怨歎者。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang aided Bei in governing Shu, greatly favoring severity; many people complained.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang helped Bei govern Shu with a notably stern hand, and many grumbled against it.

sentences.zh: 法正謂亮曰：「昔高祖入關，約法三章，秦民知德。

translations.literal: Fa Zheng said to Liang: "In the past Gaozu entered the passes, made the three-article law, and the Qin people knew his virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Fa Zheng told Liang, "When Gaozu entered the passes, he proclaimed the three-article law, and the people of Qin felt his virtue."

sentences.zh: 今君假借威力，跨據一州，初有其國，未垂惠撫；

translations.literal: Now you borrow authority, straddle one province, have just gained a state, and have not yet bestowed gracious rule;
translations.idiomatic: You now wield borrowed power across a whole province, have only just gained a state, and have not yet shown gracious rule;

sentences.zh: 且客主之義，宜相降下，願緩刑弛禁以慰其望。

translations.literal: moreover the guest-host relationship should be mutually lowering; I wish you would ease punishments and relax prohibitions to comfort their hopes."
translations.idiomatic: and as guest among hosts you ought to show forbearance. Ease punishments and relax prohibitions to satisfy what the people hope for."

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「君知其一，未知其二。

translations.literal: " Liang said: "You know the first part but not the second."
translations.idiomatic: " Liang replied, "You know one side of this, not the other."

sentences.zh: 秦以無道，政苛民怨，匹夫大呼，天下土崩；

translations.literal: Qin was without the Way, government harsh and the people resentful; a common man shouted once and the realm collapsed;
translations.idiomatic: Qin ruled without the Way, its government harsh and the people full of resentment. One common man cried out and the realm fell apart;

sentences.zh: 高祖因之，可以弘濟。

translations.literal: Gaozu took advantage of this and could broadly rescue the age.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu seized that moment and could bring broad relief to the age.

sentences.zh: 劉璋闇弱，自焉已來，有累世之累，文法羈縻，互相承奉，德政不舉，威刑不肅。

translations.literal: Liu Zhang was dim and weak; since Liu Yan's time there had been burdens of many generations, written law binding and restraining, mutual obeisance, virtuous government not raised, awe-inspiring punishments not enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang was weak and muddled. Since Liu Yan's day burdens had piled up for generations, written law had become mere shackles, officials merely bowed to one another, virtuous rule went unpracticed, and awe-inspiring punishments went unenforced.

sentences.zh: 蜀土人土，專權自恣，君臣之道，漸以陵替。

translations.literal: The gentry of Shu held power and indulged themselves; the way of ruler and minister gradually was overturned.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's local elites seized power and did as they pleased, and the bond between ruler and minister was steadily overturned.

sentences.zh: 寵之以位，位極則賤；

translations.literal: Honor them with rank, and when rank reaches its limit they are despised;
translations.idiomatic: Honor men with rank, and when rank reaches its limit they grow contemptible;

sentences.zh: 順之以恩，恩竭則慢。

translations.literal: indulge them with favor, and when favor is exhausted they grow insolent.
translations.idiomatic: indulge them with favor, and when favor is exhausted they grow insolent.

sentences.zh: 所以致敝，實由於此。

translations.literal: The reason for reaching ruin truly lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: The decay they brought about came chiefly from this.

sentences.zh: 吾今威之以法，法行則知恩；

translations.literal: I now awe them with law; when law is enforced they know favor;
translations.idiomatic: I now awe them with law; when law is enforced they learn what favor means;

sentences.zh: 限之以爵，爵加則知榮。

translations.literal: limit them with noble rank; when rank is added they know glory.
translations.idiomatic: limit them with noble rank; when rank is granted they learn what glory means.

sentences.zh: 榮恩並濟，上下有節，為治之要，於斯而著矣。

translations.literal: Glory and favor both applied, superior and inferior having measure—this is the key to governance, and here it is made clear."
translations.idiomatic: Glory and favor working together, superior and inferior kept in their proper measure—that is the heart of good government, and here it stands plain."

sentences.zh: 劉備以零陵蔣琬為廣都長。

translations.literal: Liu Bei made Jiang Wan of Lingling Magistrate of Guangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei appointed Jiang Wan of Lingling magistrate of Guangdu.

sentences.zh: 備嘗因遊觀，奄至廣都，見琬眾事不治，時又沉醉。

translations.literal: Bei once while out touring suddenly arrived at Guangdu, saw Wan's many affairs untended, and that he was at the time drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Once while out on an inspection tour, Bei suddenly appeared at Guangdu and found Wan's affairs in disorder and Wan himself drunk.

sentences.zh: 備大怒，將加罪戮。

translations.literal: Bei was greatly angered and was about to punish him with death.
translations.idiomatic: Bei flew into a rage and was about to have him executed.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮請曰：「蔣琬社稷之器，非百里之才也。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang pleaded: "Jiang Wan is a vessel of state, not talent for a hundred-li district."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang pleaded, "Jiang Wan is fit to serve the state—he is no mere district administrator."

sentences.zh: 其為政以安民為本，不以修飾為先，願主公重加察之。

translations.literal: His governing takes securing the people as root, not ornament as first; I wish the lord would examine him again carefully."
translations.idiomatic: He governs to secure the people, not to put on a show. I beg you to look at him again with care."

sentences.zh: 」備雅敬亮，乃不加罪，倉卒但免官而已。

translations.literal: " Bei greatly respected Liang, so did not punish him, but in haste merely dismissed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: " Bei held Liang in high regard, so he did not punish Wan but merely stripped him of office in haste.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，魏公操擊孫權，留少子臨菑侯植守鄴。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, Duke Cao attacked Sun Quan, leaving his youngest son Marquis of Linzi Zhi to guard Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, during the seventh month, Duke Cao attacked Sun Quan and left his youngest son, Marquis of Linzi Cao Zhi, to guard Ye.

sentences.zh: 操為諸子高選官屬，以刑顒為植家丞。

translations.literal: Cao for his sons carefully selected staff, making Xing Yong Zhi's household aide.
translations.idiomatic: Cao carefully chose staff for his sons and made Xing Yong household aide to Zhi.

sentences.zh: 顒防閒以禮，無所屈撓，由是不合。

translations.literal: Yong guarded and restrained him with ritual propriety, yielding in nothing, and for this reason they did not get along.
translations.idiomatic: Yong kept him in check with strict ritual propriety and would not bend, and for that reason they did not get along.

sentences.zh: 庶子劉楨美文辭，植親愛之。

translations.literal: Associate Liu Zhen had fine literary style; Zhi was fond of him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhen, a junior associate, wrote fine prose, and Zhi was fond of him.

sentences.zh: 楨以書諫植曰：「君侯采庶子之春華，忘家丞之秋實，為上招謗，其罪不小，愚實懼焉。

translations.literal: Zhen admonished Zhi in a letter: "Your Lordship gathers the associate's spring flowers but forgets the household aide's autumn fruit—this invites slander from above, and the fault is no small one; I truly fear it."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen wrote to admonish Zhi, "You gather the spring blossoms your junior offers but forget the autumn fruit your household aide provides. You invite your father's reproach, and the fault is no small one. I am truly afraid for you."

sentences.zh: 魏尚書令荀攸卒。

translations.literal: Wei Director of the Masters of Writing Xun You died.
translations.idiomatic: Xun You, Director of the Masters of Writing in Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 攸深密有智防，自從魏公操攻討，常謀謨帷幄，時人及子弟莫知其所言。

translations.literal: You was deeply secretive and possessed strategic foresight; from the time he followed Duke Cao in campaigns he often plotted within the curtain; people of the time and even his sons and younger brothers did not know what he said.
translations.idiomatic: You was deeply secretive and possessed keen strategic foresight. From the time he followed Duke Cao on campaign he often plotted behind closed curtains, and neither his contemporaries nor even his own sons knew what he had said.

sentences.zh: 操嘗稱：「荀文若之進善，不進不休；

translations.literal: Cao once praised: "Xun Wenruo's advancing the good—he does not advance and then stop;"
translations.idiomatic: Cao once said, "Xun Wenruo advances the good and never stops until it is done;

sentences.zh: 荀公達之去惡，不去不止。

translations.literal: Xun Gongda's removing evil—he does not remove and then stop."
translations.idiomatic: Xun Gongda removes evil and never stops until it is gone."

sentences.zh: 」又稱：「二荀令之論人，久而益信，吾沒世不忘。

translations.literal: " He also praised: "The two Director Xuns' judging of men—over time one trusts them more; I will not forget them to my dying day."
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "The two Director Xuns judged men so well that over time one trusts them all the more. I shall not forget them as long as I live."

sentences.zh: 初，枹罕宋建因涼州亂，自號河首平漢王，改元，置百官，三十餘年。

translations.literal: Initially, Song Jian of Baohan, taking advantage of Liangzhou's disorder, styled himself King Who Pacifies Han at the River's Head, changed the era name, set up the hundred offices—for more than thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Song Jian of Baohan had exploited the disorders in Liangzhou to style himself King Who Pacifies Han at the River's Head, change the era name, and set up a full bureaucracy—for more than thirty years.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，魏公操使夏侯淵自興國討建，圍枹罕，拔之，斬建。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, Duke Cao sent Xiahou Yuan from Xingguo to attack Jian, besieged Baohan, took it, and beheaded Jian.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, during the tenth month, Duke Cao sent Xiahou Yuan from Xingguo against Jian, besieged Baohan, took it, and beheaded Jian.

sentences.zh: 淵別遣張郃等渡河，入小湟中，河西諸羌皆降，隴右平。

translations.literal: Yuan separately sent Zhang He and others across the river into Lesser Huangzhong; the Di of Hexi all surrendered, and Longyou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan separately sent Zhang He and others across the river into Lesser Huangzhong; the Qiang west of the river all submitted, and Longyou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 帝自都許以來，守位而已，左右侍衛莫非曹氏之人者。

translations.literal: Since the Emperor had his capital at Xu, he merely kept his place; those attending and guarding him on left and right were none but men of the Cao clan.
translations.idiomatic: Since the emperor had his court at Xu, he had held nothing but an empty throne; every attendant and guard around him was a man of the Cao clan.

sentences.zh: 議郎趙彥嘗為帝陳言時策，魏公操惡而殺之。

translations.literal: Gentleman Consultant Zhao Yan once presented timely policy to the Emperor; Duke Cao hated this and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman Consultant Zhao Yan once laid out timely policy for the emperor; Duke Cao hated it and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 操後以事入見殿中，帝不任其懼，因曰：「君若能相輔，則厚；

translations.literal: Cao later entered the hall on business; the Emperor, unable to bear his dread, therefore said: "If you can assist me, the reward will be great;"
translations.idiomatic: Cao later came into the hall on business. The emperor, unable to master his fear, said, "If you can truly assist me, the reward will be great;

sentences.zh: 不爾，幸垂恩相捨。

translations.literal: if not, I beg you graciously to let me go."
translations.idiomatic: if not, I beg you graciously to let me go."

sentences.zh: 」操失色，俛仰求出。

translations.literal: " Cao lost color, bowed and looked up, and begged to leave.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao turned pale, bowed his head, and begged to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 舊儀：三公領兵，朝見，令虎賁執刃挾之。

translations.literal: Old ritual: when the Three Excellencies leading troops came to court audience, tiger guards were ordered to hold blades and flank them.
translations.idiomatic: By old ritual, when the Three Excellencies who commanded troops came to audience, tiger guards were ordered to flank them with blades drawn.

sentences.zh: 操出，顧左右，汗流浹背；

translations.literal: Cao went out, looked back at those left and right, sweat streaming down his back;
translations.idiomatic: Cao went out, glanced back at his attendants, sweat streaming down his back;

sentences.zh: 自後不復朝請。

translations.literal: from then on he no longer came to court audience.
translations.idiomatic: and from then on he never came to court audience again.

sentences.zh: 董承女為貴人，操誅承，求貴人殺之。

translations.literal: Dong Cheng's daughter was a Noble Lady; Cao executed Cheng and demanded the Noble Lady be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Cheng's daughter had been made a Noble Lady. Cao executed Cheng and demanded that the Noble Lady be killed as well.

sentences.zh: 帝以貴人有妊，累為請，不能得。

translations.literal: The Emperor because the Noble Lady was pregnant repeatedly pleaded, but could not obtain this.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Noble Lady was pregnant, the emperor pleaded again and again, but could not save her.

sentences.zh: 伏皇后由是懷懼，乃與父完書，言曹操殘逼之狀，令密圖之，完不敢發。

translations.literal: Empress Fu from this grew fearful; she then wrote her father Wan, describing Cao's cruel oppression, ordering him to plot secretly; Wan did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Fu was seized with fear and wrote her father Wan describing Cao's cruel oppression, urging him to plot in secret. Wan did not dare act.

sentences.zh: 至是，事乃洩，操大怒，十一月，使御史大夫郗慮持節策收皇后璽綬，以尚書令華歆為副，勒兵入宮，收後。

translations.literal: At this time the affair leaked out; Cao was greatly angered. Eleventh month, he sent Grandee Secretary Xi Lü bearing credentials to seize the Empress's seal and sash, with Director of the Masters of Writing Hua Xin as deputy, leading troops into the palace to seize the Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Now the affair leaked out, and Cao was furious. In the eleventh month he sent Grandee Secretary Xi Lü with credentials to seize the empress's seal and sash, with Director of the Masters of Writing Hua Xin as his deputy, and led troops into the palace to take her.

sentences.zh: 後閉戶，藏壁中。

translations.literal: The Empress shut her door and hid in the wall.
translations.idiomatic: The empress shut her door and hid inside the wall.

sentences.zh: 歆壞戶發壁，就牽後出。

translations.literal: Xin broke the door, opened the wall, and dragged the Empress out.
translations.idiomatic: Xin broke down the door, tore open the wall, and dragged the empress out.

sentences.zh: 時帝在外殿，引慮於坐，後被發，徒跣，行泣，過訣曰：「不能復相活邪？

translations.literal: The Emperor was then in the outer hall and drew Lü to sit with him; the Empress's hair was loose, she went barefoot, walked weeping, passed by in farewell and said: "Can you not keep me alive after all?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was in the outer hall and had drawn Lü to sit beside him. The empress came with her hair loose and barefoot, weeping as she passed. She took her leave and said, "Can you not save my life after all?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「我亦不知命在何時！

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "I too do not know when my life will end!"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I too do not know when my own life will end!"

sentences.zh: 」顧謂慮曰：「郗公，天下寧有是邪！

translations.literal: " He turned and said to Lü: "Lord Xi, can there truly be such a thing under heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: " He turned to Lü and said, "Lord Xi, can such a thing truly exist under heaven!"

sentences.zh: 」遂將後下暴室，以幽死；

translations.literal: " They then took the Empress down to the harsh chamber and killed her by confinement;
translations.idiomatic: " They took the empress down to the harsh chamber and killed her by confinement;

sentences.zh: 所生二皇子，皆鴆殺之，兄弟及宗族死者百餘人。

translations.literal: the two princes she had borne were all poisoned to death; brothers and clansmen who died numbered more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: the two princes she had borne were poisoned to death, and more than a hundred of her brothers and kinsmen were killed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，魏公操至孟津。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Duke Cao reached Meng Ford.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Duke Cao reached Meng Ford.

sentences.zh: 操以尚書郎高柔為理曹掾。

translations.literal: Cao made Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Gao Rou clerk of the justice bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Cao made Gao Rou, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, clerk of the justice bureau.

sentences.zh: 舊法：軍征士亡，考竟其妻子。

translations.literal: Old law: when soldiers deserted on campaign, their wives and children were investigated to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old law, when soldiers deserted on campaign, their wives and children were punished to the full extent of the law.

sentences.zh: 而亡者猶不息。

translations.literal: Yet deserters still did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet desertions still did not stop.

sentences.zh: 操欲更重其刑，並及父母、兄弟，柔啟曰：「士卒亡軍，誠在可疾，然竊聞基中時有悔者。

translations.literal: Cao wished to make the punishment heavier, extending to parents and brothers; Rou submitted: "Soldiers deserting the army are indeed to be detested, yet I have heard that among them there are sometimes those who repent."
translations.idiomatic: Cao wished to make the punishment heavier, extending it to parents and brothers as well. Rou submitted, "Desertion is indeed detestable, yet I have heard that some deserters later repent."

sentences.zh: 愚謂乃宜貸其妻子，一可使誘其還心。

translations.literal: I deem it fitting to pardon their wives and children—this can lure their hearts to return.
translations.idiomatic: I believe their wives and children ought to be spared—this may lure them back.

sentences.zh: 正如前科，固已絕其意望；

translations.literal: As with the former statute, that already cut off their hope;
translations.idiomatic: The former statute already cut off their hope of return;

sentences.zh: 而猥復重之，柔恐自今在軍之士，見一人亡逃，誅將及己，亦且相隨而走，不可復得殺也。

translations.literal: yet if we rashly make it heavier, Rou fears that from now on soldiers in the army, seeing one man desert and punishment reach themselves, will also flee together—then they cannot be killed to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: yet if you rashly make it heavier, I fear that from now on, whenever a soldier sees one man desert and knows punishment will reach his own kin, the rest will flee together as well—and then you will never be able to stop them by killing.

sentences.zh: 此重刑非所以止亡，乃所以益走耳！

translations.literal: This heavy punishment is not the means to stop desertion—it is the means to increase flight!"
translations.idiomatic: Heavy punishment will not stop desertion—it will only make men run all the faster!"

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「善！

translations.literal: " Cao said: "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: " Cao said, "Well said!"

sentences.zh: 」即止不殺。

translations.literal: " He then stopped and did not kill them.
translations.idiomatic: " He then halted the killings.

sentences.zh: 孝獻皇帝壬建安二十年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xian of Han [ren], Jian'an year twenty (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xian of Han, twentieth year of Jian'an (

sentences.zh: 乙未，公元二一五年）

translations.literal: yiwei, AD 215)
translations.idiomatic: yiwei, the year 215 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲子，立貴人曹氏為皇后；

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day jiazi, the Noble Lady of the Cao clan was established as Empress;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day jiazi of the first month, the Noble Lady of the Cao clan was made empress;

sentences.zh: 魏公操之女也。

translations.literal: she was Duke Cao's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: she was Duke Cao's daughter.

sentences.zh: 三月，魏公操自將擊張魯，將自武都入氐，氐人塞道，遣張郃、朱靈等攻破之。

translations.literal: Third month, Duke Cao personally led the attack on Zhang Lu, intending to enter the Di from Wudu; the Di blocked the road; he sent Zhang He, Zhu Ling, and others to break through.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Duke Cao led the attack on Zhang Lu in person, intending to enter Di territory from Wudu. The Di blocked the road, and he sent Zhang He, Zhu Ling, and others to break through.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，操自陳倉出散關至河池，氐王竇茂眾萬餘人恃險不服，五月，攻屠之。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, Cao left Chencang through Sans Pass to Hechi; the Di king Dou Mao with more than ten thousand men relied on the terrain and would not submit; fifth month, he attacked and slaughtered them.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, during the fourth month, Cao left Chencang through Sans Pass for Hechi. The Di king Dou Mao, with more than ten thousand men, held the terrain and refused submission. In the fifth month Cao attacked and slaughtered them.

sentences.zh: 四平、金城諸將麴演、蔣石等共斬送韓遂首。

translations.literal: The generals of Siping and Jincheng, Qu Yan, Jiang Shi, and others jointly beheaded Han Sui and sent his head.
translations.idiomatic: The generals Qu Yan and Jiang Shi of Siping and Jincheng jointly beheaded Han Sui and sent his head.

sentences.zh: 初，劉備在荊州，周瑜、甘寧等數勸孫權取蜀。

translations.literal: Initially, when Liu Bei was in Jingzhou, Zhou Yu, Gan Ning, and others repeatedly urged Sun Quan to take Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Liu Bei was in Jingzhou, Zhou Yu, Gan Ning, and others repeatedly urged Sun Quan to seize Shu.

sentences.zh: 權遣使謂備曰：「劉璋不武，不能自守，若使曹操得蜀，則荊州危矣。

translations.literal: Quan sent an envoy to tell Bei: "Liu Zhang is not martial and cannot hold his own; if Cao Cao obtains Shu, then Jingzhou will be in peril."
translations.idiomatic: Quan sent an envoy to tell Bei, "Liu Zhang is no warrior and cannot hold his ground. If Cao Cao takes Shu, Jingzhou will be in peril."

sentences.zh: 今欲先攻取璋，次取張魯，一統南方，雖有十操，無所憂也。

translations.literal: Now I wish first to attack and take Zhang, next take Zhang Lu, unify the south—though there were ten Caos, there would be nothing to worry about."
translations.idiomatic: I mean to take Zhang first, then Zhang Lu, and unify the south. Even ten Caos could not trouble us then."

sentences.zh: 」備報曰：「益州民富地險，劉璋雖弱，足以自守。

translations.literal: " Bei replied: "Yizhou's people are rich and its land perilous; though Liu Zhang is weak, he is enough to hold his own."
translations.idiomatic: " Bei replied, "Yizhou is rich in people and perilous in terrain. Though Liu Zhang is weak, he can still hold his own."

sentences.zh: 今暴師於蜀、漢，轉運於萬里，欲使戰克攻取，舉不失利，此孫、吳所難也。

translations.literal: Now to expose the army in Shu and Han, transport supplies ten thousand li, and expect every battle won and every attack taken without loss—this is what Sun Wu would find difficult."
translations.idiomatic: To expose your army in Shu and Han, haul supplies ten thousand li, and expect every battle won without loss—that is what even Sun Wu would find hard."

sentences.zh: 議者見曹操失利於赤壁，謂其力屈，無復遠念。

translations.literal: Debaters seeing Cao defeated at Red Cliffs say his strength is bent and he has no further distant designs.
translations.idiomatic: Men who saw Cao defeated at Red Cliffs say his strength is spent and he has no further distant ambitions.

sentences.zh: 今操三分天下已有其二，將欲飲馬於滄海，觀兵於吳會，何肯守此坐須老乎！

translations.literal: Now Cao already has two parts of the three-part realm; he will wish to water his horses at the blue sea and review troops at Wu and Kuaiji—how would he be willing to sit here and wait to grow old!"
translations.idiomatic: Cao already holds two thirds of the realm. He means to water his horses at the eastern sea and parade his troops at Wu and Kuaiji. Why would he sit here growing old!"

sentences.zh: 而同盟無故自相攻伐，借樞於操，使敵承其隙，非長計也。

translations.literal: Yet the alliance for no reason attacks one another, lending a pivot to Cao and letting the enemy seize the gap—this is no long-term plan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet allies attack one another for no reason, handing Cao an opening and letting the enemy exploit the breach—that is no long-term plan.

sentences.zh: 且備與璋托為宗室，冀憑英靈以匡漢朝。

translations.literal: Moreover Bei and Zhang claim kinship as imperial clansmen, hoping to rely on ancestral spirits to restore the Han house.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Zhang and I claim kinship as imperial clansmen and hope to rely on our ancestors' spirits to restore the Han.

sentences.zh: 今璋得罪於左右，備獨悚懼，非所敢聞，願加寬貸。

translations.literal: Now Zhang has offended your court; Bei alone is fearful and trembling—this is not what I dare hear; I wish you would add lenient pardon."
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhang has given offense to your court. I am fearful and trembling at the very thought, and I beg you to show him leniency."

sentences.zh: 」權不聽，遣孫瑜率水軍往夏口。

translations.literal: " Quan did not listen and sent Sun Yu leading the water army toward Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: " Quan would not listen and sent Sun Yu with the fleet toward Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 備不聽軍過，謂瑜曰：「汝欲取蜀，吾當被髪入山，不失信於天下也。

translations.literal: Bei would not let the army pass and told Yu: "If you wish to take Shu, I shall let my hair down and enter the mountains—I will not fail in faith to the world."
translations.idiomatic: Bei would not let the army pass and told Yu, "If you mean to take Shu, I shall let down my hair and go into the mountains—I will not break faith with the world."

sentences.zh: 」使關羽屯江陵，張飛屯秭歸，諸葛亮據南郡，備自住孱陵，權不得已召瑜還。

translations.literal: " He stationed Guan Yu at Jiangling, Zhang Fei at Zigui, Zhuge Liang holding Nan commandery, Bei himself residing at Chanling; Quan had no choice but to recall Yu.
translations.idiomatic: " He posted Guan Yu at Jiangling, Zhang Fei at Zigui, and Zhuge Liang in Nan commandery, while he himself held Chanling. Quan had no choice but to recall Yu.

sentences.zh: 及備西攻劉璋，權曰：「猾虜，乃敢挾詐如此！

translations.literal: When Bei attacked Liu Zhang in the west, Quan said: "Crafty barbarian—he dares use deceit like this!"
translations.idiomatic: When Bei marched west against Liu Zhang, Quan said, "That crafty barbarian—he dared deceive us like this!"

sentences.zh: 」備留關羽守江陵，魯肅與羽鄰界；

translations.literal: " Bei left Guan Yu to guard Jiangling; Lu Su was stationed on a border adjoining Yu;
translations.idiomatic: " Bei posted Guan Yu at Jiangling while Lu Su held a neighboring frontier post against him;

sentences.zh: 羽數生疑貳，肅常以歡好撫之。

translations.literal: Yu repeatedly harbored doubts of disloyalty; Su always soothed him with friendly goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu kept nursing suspicions of treachery, but Lu Su always placated him with cordial gestures.

sentences.zh: 及備已得益州，權令中司馬諸葛瑾以備求荊州諸郡。

translations.literal: When Bei had already obtained Yizhou, Quan ordered Central Major Zhuge Jin to ask Bei on his behalf for the commanderies of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once Bei had taken Yizhou, Quan sent Central Major Zhuge Jin to demand that Bei return the Jingzhou commanderies.

sentences.zh: 備不許，曰：「吾方圖涼州，涼州定，乃盡以荊州相與耳。

translations.literal: Bei did not consent and said: "I am just now planning Liangzhou; when Liangzhou is settled, then I shall turn over all of Jingzhou to you.
translations.idiomatic: Bei refused and said, "I am campaigning for Liangzhou now; once Liangzhou is secure, I will give you all of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 」權曰：「此假而不反，乃欲以虛辭引歲也。

translations.literal: " Quan said: "This is lending without returning—you only wish to use empty words to buy years.
translations.idiomatic: " Quan said, "That is a loan you never mean to repay—you only want empty promises to stall for time.

sentences.zh: 」遂置長沙、零陵、桂陽三郡長吏。

translations.literal: " He then appointed chief officials for the three commanderies of Changsha, Lingling, and Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: " He proceeded to install magistrates in Changsha, Lingling, and Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 關羽盡逐之。

translations.literal: Guan Yu drove them all out.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu expelled every one of them.

sentences.zh: 權大怒，遣呂蒙督兵二萬以取三郡。

translations.literal: Quan was greatly angered and sent Lü Meng to command twenty thousand troops to take the three commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Quan dispatched Lü Meng at the head of twenty thousand men to seize the three commanderies.

sentences.zh: 蒙移書長沙、桂陽，皆望風歸服，惟零陵太守郝普城守不降。

translations.literal: Meng sent letters to Changsha and Guiyang; both submitted at the news; only Lingling Administrator Hao Pu held the city and would not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Meng sent summons to Changsha and Guiyang, and both capitulated at once; only Hao Pu, administrator of Lingling, shut himself in the city and refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 劉備聞之，自蜀親至公安，遣關羽爭三郡。

translations.literal: Liu Bei heard of it, came in person from Shu to Gong'an, and sent Guan Yu to contest the three commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei heard, he hurried from Shu to Gong'an in person and sent Guan Yu to fight for the three commanderies.

sentences.zh: 孫權進住陸口，為諸軍節度；

translations.literal: Sun Quan advanced and encamped at Lukou to direct all the armies;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan moved up to Lukou to take overall command of the armies;

sentences.zh: 使魯肅將萬人屯曾陽以拒羽；

translations.literal: he sent Lu Su leading ten thousand men to garrison Zengyang to resist Yu;
translations.idiomatic: he posted Lu Su with ten thousand men at Zengyang to block Guan Yu;

sentences.zh: 飛書召呂蒙，使捨零陵急還助肅。

translations.literal: An urgent dispatch summoned Lü Meng, ordering him to abandon Lingling and hurry back to aid Su.
translations.idiomatic: He sent an urgent message ordering Lü Meng to drop the siege of Lingling and rush back to reinforce Lu Su.

sentences.zh: 蒙得書，秘之，夜，召諸將授以方略；

translations.literal: Meng received the letter, kept it secret, and at night summoned the generals and handed them the plan;
translations.idiomatic: Meng received the order, told no one, and that night gathered his officers to lay out his strategy;

sentences.zh: 晨，當攻零陵，顧謂郝普故人南陽鄧玄之曰：「郝子太聞世間有忠義事，亦欲為之，而不知時也。

translations.literal: At dawn, just as he was about to attack Lingling, he turned and said to Hao Pu's old friend Deng Xuanzhi of Nanyang: "Hao Zitai has heard that there are loyal and righteous deeds in the world and also wishes to perform them, yet he does not know the times.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn, on the eve of the assault on Lingling, he turned to Deng Xuanzhi of Nanyang, an old friend of Hao Pu, and said, "Zitai has heard of loyal deeds and wants to do one himself, but he does not understand the moment.

sentences.zh: 今左將軍在漢中為夏侯淵所圍；

translations.literal: Now the Left General is besieged at Hanzhong by Xiahou Yuan;
translations.idiomatic: The Left General is now trapped in Hanzhong by Xiahou Yuan;

sentences.zh: 關羽在南郡，至尊身自臨之。

translations.literal: Yu is in Nan commandery, and the Sovereign is personally facing him.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu is in Nan commandery, and the Sovereign himself is on the scene against him.

sentences.zh: 彼方首尾倒縣，救死不給，豈有餘力復營此哉！

translations.literal: They are at their wits' end, head and tail hanging inverted, barely able to save themselves from death—how could they spare strength to rescue this place!
translations.idiomatic: They are caught in a desperate crisis and can barely save themselves—how could they spare the strength to relieve you here!

sentences.zh: 今吾計力度慮而以攻此，曾不移日而城必破，城破之後，身死，何益於事，而令百歲老母戴白受誅，豈不痛哉！

translations.literal: If I now measure strength and plan carefully to attack this place, the city will fall within a day; after the city falls, if you die, what good will it do, and to make a hundred-year-old mother with white hair suffer execution—is that not painful!
translations.idiomatic: If I attack as planned, this city will fall within a day; when it falls, your death will serve no purpose, and your white-haired mother will be executed—is that not heartbreaking!

sentences.zh: 度此家不得外問，謂援可恃，故至於此耳。

translations.literal: I reckon this household cannot receive outside news and thinks aid can be relied on, hence it has come to this.
translations.idiomatic: I suppose his family has no word from outside and believes relief is coming—that is why things have reached this point.

sentences.zh: 君可見之，為陳禍福。

translations.literal: You may go see him and explain the blessings and disasters for him.
translations.idiomatic: Go see him and lay out the consequences for him.

sentences.zh: 」玄之見普，具宣蒙意，普懼而出降。

translations.literal: " Xuanzhi went to see Pu, fully declared Meng's meaning, and Pu, in fear, came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuanzhi visited Pu, delivered Meng's message in full, and Pu, frightened, came out and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 蒙迎，執其手與俱下船，語畢，出書示之，因拊手大笑。

translations.literal: Meng received him, took his hand and went down to the boat together; when the talk was finished, he produced the letter and showed it to him, then clapped his hands and laughed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Meng welcomed him, took his hand, and led him aboard a boat; when they had finished speaking, he produced the letter and showed it to him, then clapped his hands and laughed.

sentences.zh: 普見書，知備在公安而羽在益陽，慚恨入地。

translations.literal: When Pu saw the letter, he learned that Bei was at Gong'an while Yu was at Yiyang; shame and remorse made him wish to sink into the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the letter, Pu learned that Liu Bei was at Gong'an and Guan Yu at Yiyang, and he was overwhelmed with shame.

sentences.zh: 蒙留孫河，委以後事，即日引軍赴益陽。

translations.literal: Meng left Sun He behind, entrusting him with subsequent affairs, and that same day led the army toward Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Meng left Sun He in charge and marched that same day for Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 魯肅欲與關羽會語，諸將疑恐有變，議不可往。

translations.literal: Lu Su wished to meet Guan Yu for a talk; the generals suspected there might be treachery and argued that he should not go.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su wanted to meet Guan Yu face to face, but the other generals feared a trap and urged him not to go.

sentences.zh: 肅曰：「今日之事，宜相開譬。

translations.literal: Su said: "In today's matter, we ought to open matters to each other and explain clearly.
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "In a crisis like this, we should speak plainly to one another.

sentences.zh: 劉備負國，是非未決，羽亦何敢重欲干命！

translations.literal: Liu Bei has failed the alliance; right and wrong are not yet settled; how would Yu dare again to overstep his authority!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei has wronged the alliance, and the rights of the case are unsettled—how would Guan Yu dare to overstep his authority again!

sentences.zh: 」乃邀羽相見，各駐兵馬百步上，但諸將軍單刀俱會。

translations.literal: " He then invited Yu to meet; each stationed horses and troops a hundred paces away; only the generals met, each with a single saber.
translations.idiomatic: " He then invited Guan Yu to a meeting; both sides kept their troops a hundred paces back, and the two generals alone came forward, each carrying only a single blade.

sentences.zh: 肅因責數羽以不返三郡，羽曰：「烏林之役，左將軍身在行間，戮力破敵，豈得徒勞，無一塊土，而足下來欲收地邪！

translations.literal: Su thereupon reproached Yu for not returning the three commanderies; Yu said: "At the Battle of Wulin, the Left General was in the ranks himself, exerting strength together to defeat the enemy—how can we have toiled in vain without gaining a plot of land, while you come now wanting to seize territory!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su upbraided Guan Yu for withholding the three commanderies. Guan Yu replied, "At Wulin the Left General fought in the front lines and broke the enemy at our side—are we to have shed blood for nothing and gained not a foot of soil, while you now come to seize our land!

sentences.zh: 」肅曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Su said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Su said, "That is not so.

sentences.zh: 始與豫州覲於長阪，豫州之眾不當一校，計窮慮極，志勢摧弱，圖欲遠竄，望不及此。

translations.literal: At first I met the Governor of Yu at Changban; Yu's forces did not equal a single camp; his plans were exhausted and thoughts at an end, his resolve and momentum broken and weak; he plotted to flee far off—I never looked to reach this point.
translations.idiomatic: When I first met the Governor of Yu at Changban, his forces barely filled a single camp; he was spent and broken in spirit and meant to flee into the distance—I never imagined things would come to this.

sentences.zh: 主上矜愍豫州之身無有處所，不愛土地士民之力，使有所庇廕以濟其患；

translations.literal: Our sovereign pitied that the Governor of Yu had no place for his person and did not begrudge the strength of lands, soil, and people, granting him shelter to relieve his distress;
translations.idiomatic: Our lord took pity on the Governor of Yu, who had nowhere to stand, and without stinting territory or manpower gave him shelter from his troubles;

sentences.zh: 而豫州私獨飾情，愆德墮好。

translations.literal: Yet the Governor of Yu privately alone adorned his feelings, failing in virtue and ruining goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Governor of Yu put on a show of friendship in private while breaking faith and destroying the bond between us.

sentences.zh: 今已藉手於西州矣，又欲翦並荊州之土，斯蓋凡夫所不忍行，而況整領人物之主乎！

translations.literal: Now he has already gained a foothold in the western province, yet again wishes to carve up and annex the territory of Jingzhou—this is what even an ordinary man would not bear to do, how much less a lord who governs men and affairs!
translations.idiomatic: Now that he has a foothold in the west, he seeks to carve up Jingzhou as well—a thing even a common man would shrink from, let alone a ruler who presides over others!

sentences.zh: 」羽無以答。

translations.literal: " Yu had nothing with which to reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Guan Yu had no answer.

sentences.zh: 會聞魏公操將攻漢中，劉備懼失益州，使使求和於權。

translations.literal: Just then it was heard that Duke Cao would attack Hanzhong; Liu Bei feared losing Yizhou and sent envoys to seek peace with Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Word then came that Duke Cao was about to attack Hanzhong; fearing he might lose Yizhou, Liu Bei sent envoys to sue for peace with Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 權令諸葛瑾報命，更尋盟好。

translations.literal: Quan ordered Zhuge Jin to report back and renew the search for allied friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Quan had Zhuge Jin reply and restore the alliance.

sentences.zh: 遂分荊州，以湘水為界；

translations.literal: They then divided Jingzhou, taking the Xiang River as the boundary;
translations.idiomatic: They then partitioned Jingzhou along the Xiang River;

sentences.zh: 長沙、江夏、桂陽以東屬權，南郡、零陵、武陵以西屬備。

translations.literal: east of Changsha, Jiangxia, and Guiyang belonged to Quan; west of Nan commandery, Lingling, and Wuling belonged to Bei.
translations.idiomatic: everything east of Changsha, Jiangxia, and Guiyang went to Quan, and everything west of Nan commandery, Lingling, and Wuling went to Bei.

sentences.zh: 諸葛瑾每奉使至蜀，與其弟亮但公會相見，退無私面。

translations.literal: Whenever Zhuge Jin went on mission to Shu, he and his brother Liang met only at public gatherings; in private there was no personal meeting.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Zhuge Jin went on embassy to Shu, he and his brother Liang met only in official settings and never privately face to face.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，魏公操至陽平。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Duke Cao reached Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, Duke Cao arrived at Yangping.

sentences.zh: 張魯欲舉漢中降，其弟衛不肯，率眾數萬人拒關堅守，橫山築城十餘里。

translations.literal: Zhang Lu wished to surrender Hanzhong, but his younger brother Wei refused, leading several tens of thousands to hold the pass firm and building a wall across the mountains for more than ten li.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu was ready to surrender Hanzhong, but his brother Wei refused and led tens of thousands of men to hold the passes, throwing up walls along the mountain ridges for more than ten li.

sentences.zh: 初，操承涼州從事及武都降人之辭，說「張魯易攻，陽平城下南北山相遠，不可守也」，信以為然。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cao, accepting the words of a Liangzhou attendant and a Wudu surrenderer, was told that "Zhang Lu is easy to attack; below Yangping city the north and south mountains are far apart and cannot be held," and believed it was so.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Cao had heard from a Liangzhou aide and a defector from Wudu that Zhang Lu would be easy to attack and that the ground below Yangping, with north and south mountains far apart, could not be defended—and he believed them.

sentences.zh: 及往臨履，不如所聞，乃歎曰：「他人商度，少如人意。

translations.literal: When he went in person to reconnoiter, it was not as he had heard; he then sighed and said: "Other men's reckonings rarely satisfy one's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw the ground for himself, it did not match what he had heard, and he sighed, "Other people's estimates rarely turn out as one hopes.

sentences.zh: 」攻陽平山上諸屯，山峻難登，既不時拔，士卒傷夷者多，軍食且盡，操意沮，便欲拔軍截山而還，遣大將軍夏侯惇、將軍許褚呼山上兵還。

translations.literal: " He attacked the stockades on Yangping mountain; the mountains were steep and hard to climb, and they could not quickly take them; many soldiers were wounded; army provisions were nearly exhausted; Cao's spirits were dampened, and he was about to withdraw the army and cut across the mountain to return, sending Grand General Xiahou Dun and General Xu Chu to call the troops on the mountain back.
translations.idiomatic: " He assaulted the hill forts at Yangping, but the slopes were steep and the positions held; the attack stalled, casualties mounted, and provisions ran low. Dispirited, Cao prepared to pull back across the mountains and sent Grand General Xiahou Dun and General Xu Chu to recall the men on the heights.

sentences.zh: 會前軍夜迷惑，誤入張衛別營，營中大驚退散。

translations.literal: Just then the van army lost its way at night and mistakenly entered one of Zhang Wei's separate camps; the camp was greatly alarmed and scattered in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: That night the vanguard lost its way in the dark and blundered into one of Zhang Wei's outlying camps, throwing the enemy into panic and flight.

sentences.zh: 侍中辛毘、主簿劉曄等在兵後，語惇、褚，言「官兵已據得賊要屯，賊已散走」，猶不信之。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Xin Pi, Chief Clerk Liu Ye, and others were behind the army; they told Dun and Chu, saying "Our officers have already seized the enemy's key stockade; the enemy has already scattered and fled," yet they still did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Xin Pi, Chief Clerk Liu Ye, and others, who were in the rear, told Dun and Chu that government troops had already taken the enemy's key camp and that the enemy had broken and run—but the two generals still would not believe it.

sentences.zh: 惇前自見，乃還白操，進兵攻衛，衛等夜遁。

translations.literal: Dun went forward to see for himself, then returned and reported to Cao; they advanced to attack Wei, and Wei and the others fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Dun rode forward to see for himself, then returned and reported to Cao; the army pressed the attack, and Wei fled by night.

sentences.zh: 張魯聞陽平已陷，欲降，閻圃曰：「今以迫往，功必輕；

translations.literal: Zhang Lu heard that Yangping had fallen and wished to surrender; Yan Yuan said: "If you surrender now under pressure, the merit will surely be slight;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Lu heard that Yangping had fallen, he wanted to surrender, but Yan Yuan said, "If you submit now under pressure, your merit will count for little;

sentences.zh: 不如依杜濩赴樸胡，與相拒，然後委質，功必多。

translations.literal: it would be better to join Du Hu and go to Pu Hu, resist together, and then submit allegiance—the merit will surely be great.
translations.idiomatic: better to join Du Hu and go to Pu Hu, hold out together, and then submit formally—your reward will be far greater.

sentences.zh: 」乃奔南山入巴中。

translations.literal: " He then fled south into the mountains and entered Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: " He then fled south into the mountains and withdrew into Baxi.

sentences.zh: 左右欲悉燒寶貨倉庫，魯曰：「本欲歸命國家，而意未得達。

translations.literal: Those around him wished to burn all the treasures and storehouses; Lu said: "I originally wished to submit to the state, yet my intention has not yet been fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: His followers wanted to burn all the stores of treasure, but Lu said, "I meant to surrender to the imperial court, and that aim has not yet been achieved.

sentences.zh: 今之走避銳鋒，非有惡意。

translations.literal: Our flight now is to avoid the sharp edge—there is no evil intent.
translations.idiomatic: This retreat is only to avoid the enemy's sharp edge, not out of malice.

sentences.zh: 寶貨倉庫，國家之有。

translations.literal: Treasures and storehouses belong to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Treasures and stores belong to the state.

sentences.zh: 」遂封藏而去。

translations.literal: " He then sealed and stored them and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " He had them sealed and left them behind.

sentences.zh: 操入南鄭，甚嘉之。

translations.literal: When Cao entered Nanzheng, he greatly praised this.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao entered Nanzheng, he greatly admired this conduct.

sentences.zh: 又以魯本有善意，遣人慰喻之。

translations.literal: Moreover, because Lu had originally borne good intent, he sent men to comfort and explain to him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Lu had shown good faith from the start, Cao also sent envoys to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 丞相主簿司馬懿言於操曰：「劉備以詐力虜劉璋，蜀人未附，而遠爭江陵，此機不可失也。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of the Chancellor Sima Yi spoke to Cao, saying: "Liu Bei by deceit and force captured Liu Zhang; the people of Shu are not yet attached, yet he contends far away at Jiangling—this opportunity must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Sima Yi said to Cao, "Liu Bei seized Liu Zhang by fraud and force; the people of Shu are not yet loyal to him, yet he is fighting far away at Jiangling—this is an opportunity we must not miss.

sentences.zh: 今克漢中，益州震動，進兵臨之，勢必瓦解。

translations.literal: Now that Hanzhong is taken, Yizhou will be shaken; if we advance and press upon it, the momentum will surely collapse.
translations.idiomatic: With Hanzhong in our hands, Yizhou will be shaken; if we march against it at once, it will surely fall apart.

sentences.zh: 聖人不能違時，亦不可失時也。

translations.literal: A sage cannot go against the times, nor can one miss the times.
