translations.idiomatic: Even a sage cannot defy the season, and one must not miss the moment.

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「人苦無足，既得隴，復望蜀邪！

translations.literal: " Cao said: "Men suffer from lack of contentment—having already gained Long, yet still look to Shu!
translations.idiomatic: " Cao said, "Men are never satisfied—having taken Long, you would look to Shu as well!

sentences.zh: 」劉曄曰：「劉備，人傑也，有度而遲；

translations.literal: " Liu Ye said: "Liu Bei is a hero among men—he has measure yet is slow;
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Ye said, "Liu Bei is a man of heroic stature—far-sighted but deliberate;

sentences.zh: 得蜀日淺，蜀人未恃也。

translations.literal: he has held Shu for only a short time, and the people of Shu do not yet rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: he has held Shu only briefly, and the people there do not yet trust him.

sentences.zh: 今破漢中，蜀人震恐，其勢自傾。

translations.literal: Now that Hanzhong is broken, the people of Shu will be shaken in terror and their momentum will collapse of itself.
translations.idiomatic: With Hanzhong lost, the people of Shu are terrified and his position is already crumbling.

sentences.zh: 以公之神明，因其傾而壓之，無不克也。

translations.literal: With your brilliance, if you press upon them as they collapse, there is nothing you cannot overcome.
translations.idiomatic: With your brilliance, if you press him while he is faltering, you cannot fail.

sentences.zh: 若小緩之，諸葛亮明於治國而為相，關羽、張飛勇冠三軍而為將，蜀民既定，據險守要，則不可犯矣。

translations.literal: If you relax slightly, Zhuge Liang is clear in governing the state and serves as chancellor; Guan Yu and Zhang Fei are bravest in the three armies and serve as generals; once the people of Shu are settled and hold difficult passes and guard strategic points, they cannot be violated.
translations.idiomatic: Wait even a little, and with Zhuge Liang as a brilliant administrator and chancellor and Guan Yu and Zhang Fei as the bravest generals in the land, once the people of Shu settle in and hold the mountain passes, he will become untouchable.

sentences.zh: 今不取，必為後憂。

translations.literal: If you do not take it now, it will surely become a later worry.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not strike now, you will regret it later.

sentences.zh: 」操不從。

translations.literal: " Cao did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao would not listen.

sentences.zh: 居七日，蜀降者說「蜀中一日數十驚，守將雖斬之而不能安也。

translations.literal: After seven days, a Shu surrenderer said: "In Shu there are several tens of alarms in a single day; though the defending generals execute men, they cannot restore calm.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days later a defector from Shu reported, "In Shu there are dozens of alarms in a single day; though the garrison commanders execute people, they cannot restore order.

sentences.zh: 」操問曄曰：「今尚可擊不？

translations.literal: " Cao asked Ye: "Can we still attack now?
translations.idiomatic: " Cao asked Liu Ye, "Can we still attack?

sentences.zh: 」曄曰：「今已小定，未可擊也。

translations.literal: " Ye said: "It has now settled somewhat; it cannot be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Ye said, "It has already stabilized somewhat—we cannot attack now.

sentences.zh: 」乃還。

translations.literal: " He then returned.
translations.idiomatic: " So Cao withdrew.

sentences.zh: 以夏侯淵為都護將軍，督張郃、徐晃等守漢中；

translations.literal: He made Xiahou Yuan Protector General and had him supervise Zhang He, Xu Huang, and others in guarding Hanzhong;
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Xiahou Yuan Protector General to command Zhang He, Xu Huang, and others in holding Hanzhong;

sentences.zh: 以丞相長史杜襲為駙馬都尉，留督漢中事。

translations.literal: he made Chancellor Chief Clerk Du Xi Commandant of Equipage and left him to supervise Hanzhong affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He left Chancellor Chief Clerk Du Xi as Commandant of Equipage to oversee civil affairs in Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 襲綏懷開導，百姓自樂出徙洛、鄴者八萬餘口。

translations.literal: Xi soothed and guided with kindness; more than eighty thousand common people willingly moved out to settle in Luoyang and Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xi soothed and settled the people with gentle guidance, and more than eighty thousand families willingly migrated to Luoyang and Ye.

sentences.zh: 八月，孫權率眾十萬圍合肥。

translations.literal: Eighth month: Sun Quan led a hundred thousand troops to besiege Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Sun Quan led a hundred thousand men to besiege Hefei.

sentences.zh: 時張遼、李典、樂進將七千餘人屯合肥。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Liao, Li Dian, and Yue Jin commanded a little more than seven thousand men garrisoned at Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao, Li Dian, and Yue Jin then held Hefei with a garrison of just over seven thousand men.

sentences.zh: 魏公操之征張魯也，為教與合肥護軍薛悌，署函邊曰：「賊至，乃發。

translations.literal: When Duke Cao was campaigning against Zhang Lu, he prepared instructions for Hefei Protector-of-the-Army Xue Ti, writing on the edge of the sealed packet: "Open when the enemy arrives.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Cao marched against Zhang Lu, he left sealed instructions for Hefei Protector-of-the-Army Xue Ti, marked on the envelope: "Open only when the enemy arrives.

sentences.zh: 」及權至，發教，教曰：「若孫權至者，張、李將軍出戰，樂將軍守，護軍勿得與戰。

translations.literal: " When Quan arrived, they opened the instructions; the instructions said: "If Sun Quan comes, Generals Zhang and Li shall go out to fight, General Yue shall hold the defense, and the Protector-of-the-Army must not join battle.
translations.idiomatic: " When Sun Quan arrived, they opened the packet. It read: "If Sun Quan comes, Generals Zhang and Li are to take the field, General Yue is to hold the city, and the Protector-of-the-Army must not fight.

sentences.zh: 」諸將以眾寡不敵，疑之。

translations.literal: " The generals, considering their numbers too few to match the enemy, were doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: " The generals doubted the order, seeing how badly they were outnumbered.

sentences.zh: 張遼曰：「公遠征在外，比救至，彼破我必矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Liao said: "The Duke is campaigning far away; before relief arrives, the enemy will surely break us.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao said, "The Duke is far away on campaign; before relief can arrive, the enemy will certainly destroy us.

sentences.zh: 是以教指及其未合逆擊之，折其盛勢，以安眾心，然後可守也。

translations.literal: Therefore the instructions intend that before they have joined battle we strike them in reverse, break their surging momentum, settle the soldiers' hearts, and only then can we defend.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the instructions tell us to strike before they fully deploy, break their momentum, and steady the troops—only then can we hold the city.

sentences.zh: 」進等莫對。

translations.literal: " Jin and the others had nothing to reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue Jin and the others had no answer.

sentences.zh: 遼怒曰：「成敗之機，在此一戰。

translations.literal: Liao said angrily: "The hinge of success or failure is in this one battle.
translations.idiomatic: Liao said angrily, "Victory or defeat hangs on this single battle.

sentences.zh: 諸君若疑，遼將獨決之。

translations.literal: If you gentlemen doubt, Liao alone will decide it.
translations.idiomatic: If you still hesitate, I will decide it alone.

sentences.zh: 」李典素與遼不睦，慨然曰：「此國家大事，顧君計何如耳，吾可以私憾而忘公義乎！

translations.literal: " Li Dian had long been on bad terms with Liao; he said with emotion: "This is a great matter of state—it depends only on what plan you think best; how could I let private resentment make me forget public duty!
translations.idiomatic: " Li Dian, who had never gotten along with Liao, said firmly, "This is a matter of state; I care only whether your plan is sound—how could private grudges make me forget the public good!

sentences.zh: 請從君而出。

translations.literal: I ask to follow you out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: I will go out with you.

sentences.zh: 」於是遼夜募敢從之士，得八百人，椎牛犒饗。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Liao by night recruited men daring enough to follow, got eight hundred, slaughtered oxen and feasted them.
translations.idiomatic: " That night Liao recruited eight hundred volunteers, slaughtered oxen, and feasted them.

sentences.zh: 明旦，遼被甲持戟，先登陷陣，殺數十人，斬二大將，大呼自名，沖壘入至權麾下。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day, Liao donned armor, took a halberd, led the charge and broke the formation, killed several tens of men, beheaded two major generals, shouted his own name, burst through the ramparts and entered as far as Quan's command pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day, Liao armored himself, took up his halberd, and led the charge; he killed dozens of men, cut down two enemy generals, shouted his own name, broke through the lines, and burst in as far as Sun Quan's command post.

sentences.zh: 權大驚，不知所為，走登高塚，以長戟自守。

translations.literal: Quan was greatly alarmed and did not know what to do; he fled up a high mound and defended himself with a long halberd.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan was thrown into panic; he fled to a high mound and defended himself with a long halberd.

sentences.zh: 遼叱權下戰，權不敢動，望見遼所將眾少，乃聚圍遼數重。

translations.literal: Liao shouted at Quan to come down and fight; Quan did not dare move; seeing that the troops Liao led were few, he gathered men and surrounded Liao in several rings.
translations.idiomatic: Liao shouted for Sun Quan to come down and fight, but Sun Quan did not dare move; seeing how few men Liao had brought, he gathered his forces and surrounded him in layer after layer.

sentences.zh: 遼急擊圍開，將麾下數十人得出。

translations.literal: Liao urgently attacked and opened the encirclement; leading several tens of his followers, he got out.
translations.idiomatic: Liao fought desperately to break the ring and escaped with several dozen of his men.

sentences.zh: 餘眾號呼曰：「將軍棄我乎？

translations.literal: The remaining troops cried out: "General, have you abandoned us?
translations.idiomatic: The men left behind cried out, "General, have you abandoned us?

sentences.zh: 」遼復還突圍，拔出餘眾，權人馬皆披靡，無敢當者。

translations.literal: " Liao turned back and broke through again, pulled out the remaining troops; Quan's men and horses all collapsed before him, and none dared oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: " Liao wheeled about, fought his way back in, and rescued the rest; Sun Quan's men broke before him, and none dared stand in his way.

sentences.zh: 自旦戰至日中，吳人奪氣。

translations.literal: From dawn until midday they fought; the Wu men lost their fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The battle lasted from dawn to midday, and the Wu troops lost their nerve.

sentences.zh: 乃還修守備，眾心遂安。

translations.literal: They then returned and repaired the defenses; the soldiers' hearts were thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: They then returned to shore up the defenses, and the garrison's morale was restored.

sentences.zh: 權守合肥十餘日，城不可拔，徹軍還。

translations.literal: Quan besieged Hefei for more than ten days; the city could not be taken, and he withdrew the army and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan besieged Hefei for more than ten days but could not take it and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 兵皆就路，權與諸將在逍遙津北，張遼覘望知之，即將步騎奄至。

translations.literal: The troops all took to the road; Quan and the generals were north of Xiaoyao Ford; Zhang Liao spied and learned of it, and immediately led infantry and cavalry to arrive suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: As the army marched off, Sun Quan and his officers were north of Xiaoyao Ford; Zhang Liao saw this from his scouts and immediately led infantry and cavalry in a sudden rush upon them.

sentences.zh: 甘寧與呂蒙等力戰扞敵，凌統率親近扶權出圍，復還與遼戰，左右盡死，身亦被創，度權已免，乃還。

translations.literal: Gan Ning and Lü Meng and others fought hard to repel the enemy; Ling Tong led close followers to support Quan out of the encirclement; he then returned to fight Liao again; those at his side all died, and he himself was wounded; judging that Quan was already safe, he then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ning, Lü Meng, and others fought desperately to hold the enemy back; Ling Tong led his personal guard to escort Sun Quan out of the trap, then turned back to fight Zhang Liao again; his attendants were killed to the last man and he himself was wounded, but once he saw that Sun Quan was safe, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 權乘駿馬上津橋，橋面已徹，丈餘無版；

translations.literal: Quan mounted a fine horse onto Jin Bridge; the bridge deck had already been dismantled, and for more than a zhang there were no planks;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan mounted a swift horse and rode onto Jin Bridge, but the decking had already been torn up, leaving more than a zhang without a single plank;

sentences.zh: 親近監谷利在馬後，使權持鞍緩控，利於後著鞭以助馬勢，遂得超度。

translations.literal: His close attendant and supervisor Gu Li was behind the horse; he had Quan hold the saddle and ease the reins, while Li from behind applied the whip to aid the horse's momentum, and thus managed to cross over.
translations.idiomatic: His close attendant Gu Li rode behind him, had Sun Quan grip the saddle and slacken the reins, and whipped the horse from the rear to drive it on—and so they got across.

sentences.zh: 賀齊率三千人在津南迎權，權由是得免。

translations.literal: He Qi led three thousand men south of the ford to receive Quan, and Quan thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi led three thousand men to meet Sun Quan south of the ford, and by this means Sun Quan escaped.

sentences.zh: 權入大船宴飲，賀齊下席涕泣曰：「至尊人主，常當持重，今日之事，幾致禍敗。

translations.literal: Quan entered a large ship to feast and drink; He Qi left his seat, weeping, and said: "The supreme lord and sovereign ought always to hold himself steady and grave; today's affair nearly brought disaster and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan went aboard a great ship to feast and drink. He Qi rose from his place in tears and said, "Your Majesty, a ruler should always conduct himself with weight and restraint. What happened today nearly ended in catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 群下震怖，若無天地，願以此為終身之誡！

translations.literal: Your subordinates were shaken with terror, as if there were no heaven and earth; I pray you take this as a lesson for life!
translations.idiomatic: Your officers were terrified, as though heaven and earth had collapsed. I beg you to take this as a lesson for the rest of your life!

sentences.zh: 」權自前收其淚曰：「大慚謹已刻心，非但書紳也。

translations.literal: " Quan came forward himself and wiped away his tears, saying: "Great shame—prudence is already carved in my heart; it is not merely what is written on the girdle.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan stepped forward and wiped away his tears, saying, "I am deeply ashamed. Caution is already engraved in my heart—not merely tied to my sash.

sentences.zh: 九月，巴、賨夷帥樸胡、杜濩、任約，各舉其眾來附。

translations.literal: Ninth month, the Ba and Cong tribal chiefs Pu Hu, Du Hu, and Ren Yue each led their followers to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the Ba and Cong chieftains Pu Hu, Du Hu, and Ren Yue each brought their people over in submission.

sentences.zh: 於是分巴郡，以胡為巴東太守，濩為巴西太守，約為巴郡太守，皆封列侯。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ba Commandery was divided; Hu was made Administrator of Badong, Hu Administrator of Baxi, and Yue Administrator of Ba—all were enfeoffed as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Ba Commandery was then partitioned: Pu Hu was made Administrator of Badong, Du Hu Administrator of Baxi, and Ren Yue Administrator of Ba. All three were enfeoffed as full marquises.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，始置名號侯以賞軍功。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, named-title marquis ranks were first established to reward military merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, named-title marquis ranks were established for the first time to reward military achievement.

sentences.zh: 十一月，張魯將家屬出降。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, Zhang Lu led his family out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Zhang Lu came out with his family and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 魏公操逆拜魯鎮南將軍，待以客禮，封閬中侯，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: Duke Cao of Wei met him and appointed Lu General Who Stabilizes the South, received him with guest ceremony, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Langzhong with a fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Cao went out to greet Zhang Lu, appointed him General Who Stabilizes the South, treated him as an honored guest, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Langzhong with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 封魯五子及閻圃等皆為列侯。

translations.literal: Lu's five sons and Yan Pu and others were all enfeoffed as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu's five sons, Yan Pu, and others were all enfeoffed as full marquises.

sentences.zh: 習鑿齒論曰：閻圃諫魯勿王，而曹公追封之，將來之人，孰不思順！

translations.literal: Xi Zuoshi remarked: Yan Pu advised Lu not to declare himself king, yet Duke Cao afterward enfeoffed him—with such an example before them, who in generations to come would not think to submit!
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuoshi commented: Yan Pu had urged Zhang Lu not to declare himself king, yet Duke Cao later enfeoffed him anyway. With such an example set, who in future generations would not wish to submit!

sentences.zh: 塞其本源而末流自止，其此之謂與！

translations.literal: Block the source and the downstream flow will stop of itself—is this not what is meant!
translations.idiomatic: Block the source and the downstream current stops of its own accord—is this not exactly the point!

sentences.zh: 若乃不明於此，而重焦爛之功，豐爵厚賞止於死戰之士，則民利於有亂，俗競於殺伐，阻兵杖力，干戈不戢矣。

translations.literal: If one fails to see this clearly and instead values scorched merit, lavishing titles and rich rewards only on men who die in battle, then the people will profit from disorder, custom will compete in slaughter, weapons will be relied on and force wielded, and arms will never be laid down.
translations.idiomatic: If one fails to grasp this and instead honors only charred feats of arms, reserving lofty titles and rich rewards for men who die fighting, then the people will come to profit from chaos, custom will turn to slaughter, force of arms will be exalted, and war will never end.

sentences.zh: 曹公之此封，可謂知賞罰之本矣。

translations.literal: In this enfeoffment Duke Cao may be said to have understood the root of rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In this enfeoffment, Duke Cao showed that he understood the foundation of reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 程銀、侯選、龐德皆隨魯降，魏公操復銀、選官爵，拜德立義將軍。

translations.literal: Cheng Yin, Hou Xuan, and Pang De all followed Lu in surrender; Duke Cao of Wei restored Yin and Xuan to their offices and ranks, and appointed De General Who Establishes Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yin, Hou Xuan, and Pang De all surrendered with Zhang Lu. Duke Cao restored Cheng Yin and Hou Xuan to their offices and ranks, and appointed Pang De General Who Establishes Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 張魯之走巴中也，黃權言於劉備曰：「若失漢中，則三巴不振，此為割蜀之股臂也。

translations.literal: When Zhang Lu fled into Ba, Huang Quan said to Liu Bei: "If Hanzhong is lost, the Three Ba will not be able to rally—this will be cutting off Shu's thigh and arm.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Lu fled into Ba, Huang Quan said to Liu Bei, "If we lose Hanzhong, the Three Ba will collapse. That would be cutting off Shu's very thigh and arm.

sentences.zh: 」備乃以權為護軍，率諸將迎魯；

translations.literal: " Bei thereupon made Quan Protector of the Army and led the generals to welcome Lu;
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Bei thereupon made Huang Quan Protector of the Army and led his generals out to meet Zhang Lu.

sentences.zh: 魯已降，權遂擊樸胡、杜濩、任約，破之。

translations.literal: Lu had already surrendered, so Quan then attacked Pu Hu, Du Hu, and Ren Yue and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu had already surrendered, so Huang Quan turned and attacked Pu Hu, Du Hu, and Ren Yue and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 魏公操使張郃督諸軍徇三巴，欲徙其民於漢中，進軍宕渠。

translations.literal: Duke Cao of Wei sent Zhang He to command the armies in subduing the Three Ba, intending to relocate the people to Hanzhong, and advanced the army to Dangqu.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Cao sent Zhang He to command the armies in pacifying the Three Ba, intending to relocate the population to Hanzhong, and advanced to Dangqu.

sentences.zh: 劉備使巴西太守張飛與郃相拒，五十餘日，飛襲擊郃，大破之。

translations.literal: Liu Bei sent Zhang Fei, Administrator of Baxi, to oppose He; after more than fifty days, Fei made a surprise attack on He and routed him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei sent Zhang Fei, Administrator of Baxi, to hold Zhang He at bay. After more than fifty days, Zhang Fei launched a surprise attack and routed him completely.

sentences.zh: 郃走還南鄭，備亦還成都。

translations.literal: He fled back to Nanzheng; Bei also returned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He fled back to Nanzheng, and Liu Bei also returned to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 操徙出故韓遂、馬超等兵五千餘人，使平難將軍殷署等督領，以扶風太守趙儼為關中護軍。

translations.literal: Cao relocated more than five thousand troops of the former followers of Han Sui, Ma Chao, and others, placing them under the command of Pacifying Hardship General Yin Shu and others, and making Zhao Yan, Administrator of Fufeng, Protector of the Army for Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao relocated more than five thousand troops formerly under Han Sui, Ma Chao, and others, placing them under Pacifying Hardship General Yin Shu and others, and appointed Zhao Yan, Administrator of Fufeng, Protector of the Army for Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 操使儼發千二百兵助漢中守禦，殷署督送之，行者不樂。

translations.literal: Cao had Yan dispatch twelve hundred troops to aid the Hanzhong garrison; Yin Shu supervised escorting them, and those marching were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao ordered Zhao Yan to dispatch twelve hundred troops to reinforce the Hanzhong garrison. Yin Shu supervised the escort, and the men on the march were unhappy.

sentences.zh: 儼護送至斜谷口，還，未至營，署軍叛亂。

translations.literal: Yan escorted them to the mouth of Xiegu Valley and returned; before he reached camp, Yin's army rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yan escorted them as far as the mouth of Xiegu Valley and turned back, but before he reached camp, Yin Shu's army had mutinied.

sentences.zh: 儼自隨步騎百五十人，皆叛者親黨也，聞之，各驚，被甲持兵，不復自安。

translations.literal: Yan had with him a personal escort of a hundred fifty infantry and cavalry, all close kin of the rebels; on hearing the news they were each alarmed, donned armor and took up weapons, and could no longer be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yan had with him a personal escort of a hundred and fifty foot and horse, all close kin of the mutineers. When they heard the news, each man was alarmed, donned armor, and took up weapons, unable to rest easy.

sentences.zh: 儼徐諭以成敗，慰勵懇切，皆慷慨曰：「死生當隨護軍，不敢有二！

translations.literal: Yan slowly explained success and failure to them, urging and encouraging earnestly; all said passionately: "In life and death we shall follow the Protector of the Army—we dare not waver!
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yan calmly explained the stakes to them and urged them on with earnest encouragement. All declared passionately, "In life or death we follow the Protector of the Army—we will not waver!

sentences.zh: 」前到諸營，各召料簡諸奸結叛者八百餘人，散在原野。

translations.literal: " Advancing ahead to the various camps, he summoned and inspected all who had secretly joined the rebels—more than eight hundred men—scattered across the open fields.
translations.idiomatic: " He went on ahead to the various camps, summoned and inspected more than eight hundred men who had secretly joined the mutiny, and had them dispersed across the open country.

sentences.zh: 儼下令惟取其造謀魁率治之，餘一不問，郡縣所收送皆放遣，乃即相率還降。

translations.literal: Yan ordered that only the ringleaders who planned the plot be taken and punished; the rest were not questioned at all; those captured and sent in by the commanderies and districts were all released, and they then led one another back to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yan ordered that only the chief plotters be seized and punished; the rest were not questioned at all. Those captured and sent in by the commanderies and districts were all released, and the men then led one another back in surrender.

sentences.zh: 儼密白：「宜遣將詣大營，請舊兵鎮守關中。

translations.literal: Yan secretly reported: "A general ought to be sent to the main camp to request old troops to garrison Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yan secretly reported, "A general should be sent to the main camp to request veteran troops to garrison Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 」魏公操遣將軍劉柱將二千人往，當須到乃發遣。

translations.literal: " Duke Cao of Wei sent General Liu Zhu with two thousand men to go; they were to be sent off only when he arrived.
translations.idiomatic: " Duke Cao sent General Liu Zhu with two thousand men, with orders that the troops were to be dispatched only after he arrived.

sentences.zh: 俄而事露，諸營大駭，不可安諭。

translations.literal: Before long the matter leaked out; the various camps were greatly alarmed and could not be placated with peaceful words.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the plan leaked out. The camps were thrown into panic and could no longer be calmed with gentle persuasion.

sentences.zh: 儼遂宣言：「當差留新兵之溫厚者千人，鎮守關中，其餘悉遣東。

translations.literal: Yan then proclaimed: "A selection will be made to retain a thousand of the milder new troops to garrison Guanzhong; the rest will all be sent east.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yan then announced publicly, "We will select a thousand of the steadier new recruits to remain and garrison Guanzhong; the rest will all be sent east.

sentences.zh: 」便見主者內諸營兵名籍，立差別人。

translations.literal: " He immediately saw the registrar and had the name rolls of troops in the various camps brought out, and promptly selected men to separate them.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately summoned the registrar, had the name rolls of every camp brought out, and at once began sorting the men.

sentences.zh: 留者意定，與儼同心，其當去者亦不敢動。

translations.literal: Those who were to stay had their minds settled and were of one heart with Yan; those who were to go also did not dare stir.
translations.idiomatic: Those selected to stay settled their minds and stood with Zhao Yan; those marked to leave did not dare move.

sentences.zh: 儼一日盡遣上道，因使所留千人分佈羅落之。

translations.literal: Yan in one day sent them all off on the road, then had the thousand men he retained deploy and spread cordons over them.
translations.idiomatic: In a single day Zhao Yan sent them all on their way, then deployed the thousand men he had kept back in cordons around them.

sentences.zh: 東兵尋至，乃復脅諭，並徙千人，令相及共東。

translations.literal: The eastern troops soon arrived; he then again compelled them with warnings, and relocated the thousand together, ordering them to go east in company with one another.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern troops soon arrived. He then coerced and admonished them again, moved the thousand men out together, and ordered them to travel east in one body.

sentences.zh: 凡所全致二萬餘口。

translations.literal: In all he safely delivered more than twenty thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: In all, he brought more than twenty thousand people through safely.

sentences.zh: 孝獻皇帝壬建安二十一年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xian of Han [ren], Jian'an year twenty-one (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xian of Han, twenty-first year of Jian'an (

sentences.zh: 丙申，公元二一六年）

translations.literal: bingchen, AD 216)
translations.idiomatic: bingchen, AD 216)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，魏公操還鄴。

translations.literal: Spring, second month, Duke Cao of Wei returned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring, Duke Cao returned to Ye.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，進魏公操爵為王。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month, Duke Cao of Wei was advanced in rank to king.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, Duke Cao was promoted from duke to king.

sentences.zh: 初，中尉崔琰薦巨鹿楊訓於操，操禮辟之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Commandant of the Central Guard Cui Yan had recommended Yang Xun of Julu to Cao, and Cao honored him with a summons.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Commandant of the Central Guard Cui Yan had recommended Yang Xun of Julu to Cao Cao, and Cao received him with ceremony and summoned him to office.

sentences.zh: 及操進爵，訓發表稱頌功德。

translations.literal: When Cao was advanced in rank, Xun issued a memorial praising his merit and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao was promoted in rank, Yang Xun submitted a memorial praising his merit and virtue.

sentences.zh: 或笑訓希世浮偽，謂琰為失所舉。

translations.literal: Some laughed at Xun as worldly and hypocritical, saying Yan had recommended wrongly.
translations.idiomatic: Some mocked Yang Xun as a worldly flatterer and said Cui Yan had recommended the wrong man.

sentences.zh: 琰從訓取表草視之，與訓書曰：「省表，事佳耳。

translations.literal: Yan took the draft of the memorial from Xun and looked at it, and wrote to Xun: "I have reviewed the memorial—it is well enough.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yan took the draft of the memorial from Yang Xun and read it, then wrote to him, "I have reviewed your memorial—it is well enough.

sentences.zh: 時乎，時乎！

translations.literal: Timing, timing!
translations.idiomatic: Timing, timing!

sentences.zh: 會當有變時。

translations.literal: There will surely come a time of change.
translations.idiomatic: There will surely come a time of change.

sentences.zh: 」琰本意譏論者好譴呵而不尋情理也，時有與琰宿不平者，白琰「傲世怨謗，意指不遜」，操怒，收琰付獄，髡為徒隸。

translations.literal: " Yan's original intent was to mock those who liked to denounce without seeking the reasons behind things; at the time there was one who had long been at odds with Yan, who reported that Yan was "arrogant toward the world, resentful and slanderous, his meaning disrespectful"; Cao was enraged, seized Yan and put him in prison, and had his hair cropped, making him a convict laborer.
translations.idiomatic: " Cui Yan had meant to mock those who loved to denounce others without looking into the reasons. But someone who had long borne him a grudge reported that Yan was "arrogant toward the world, resentful and slanderous, and disrespectful in his meaning." Cao Cao was enraged, seized Cui Yan, and imprisoned him, cropping his hair and reducing him to convict labor.

sentences.zh: 前白琰者復白之云：「琰為徒，對賓客虯鬚直視，若有所瞋。

translations.literal: The one who had earlier reported Yan reported again, saying: "Yan as a convict, facing guests with bristling beard and direct gaze, as if angry at something.
translations.idiomatic: The man who had reported Cui Yan before reported again, saying, "As a convict laborer, Yan faces guests with bristling beard and a direct stare, as though harboring anger.

sentences.zh: 」遂賜琰死。

translations.literal: " Yan was then ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: " Cui Yan was then ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射毛玠傷琰無辜，心不悅。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Mao Jie grieved that Yan was innocent and was displeased at heart.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Mao Jie grieved that Cui Yan was innocent and was displeased at heart.

sentences.zh: 人復白玠怨謗，操收玠付獄，侍中桓階、和洽皆為之陳理，操不聽。

translations.literal: Someone again reported that Jie was resentful and slanderous; Cao seized Jie and put him in prison; Palace Attendants Huan Jie and He Qia both pleaded his case for him, but Cao would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Someone again reported that Mao Jie was resentful and slanderous. Cao Cao seized him and imprisoned him. Palace Attendants Huan Jie and He Qia both pleaded his case, but Cao Cao would not listen.

sentences.zh: 階求案實其事。

translations.literal: Huan Jie asked to investigate and verify the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Jie asked that the matter be investigated and verified.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「言事者白，玠不但謗吾也，乃復為崔琰觖望。

translations.literal: The King said: "The informant reports that Jie not only slandered me but also harbored resentment on Cui Yan's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The King said, "The informant reports that Mao Jie not only slandered me but also nursed resentment over Cui Yan's fate.

sentences.zh: 此捐君臣恩義，妄為死友怨歎，殆不可忍也。

translations.literal: This throws away the grace and righteousness between lord and minister; to feign grief for a dead friend in reckless resentment—this can scarcely be endured.
translations.idiomatic: This casts aside the grace and duty between lord and minister, and vents reckless resentment for a dead friend—such conduct is scarcely to be borne.

sentences.zh: 」洽曰：「如言事者言，玠罪過深重，非天地所覆載。

translations.literal: " He Qia said: "If what the informant says is true, Jie's offense is heavy indeed—not what heaven and earth cover and bear.
translations.idiomatic: " He Qia said, "If what the informant says is true, Mao Jie's offense is grave indeed—beyond what heaven and earth could cover and bear.

sentences.zh: 臣非敢曲理玠以枉大倫也，以玠歷年荷寵，剛直忠公，為眾所憚，不宜有此。

translations.literal: Your subject does not dare bend the law for Jie and violate the great principle; it is that Jie has for years received favor, and being upright, loyal, and fair, he is feared by the multitude—it is not fitting that he should have this in him.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject does not dare bend the law to spare Mao Jie and violate the great moral order. But Mao Jie has enjoyed favor for years; upright, loyal, and fair, he is feared by all—and it is not fitting that he should have done such a thing.

sentences.zh: 然人情難保，要宜考玠，兩驗其實。

translations.literal: Yet human feelings are hard to guarantee; what is essential is to examine Jie and verify the truth on both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Yet human conduct is hard to guarantee. What is essential is to examine Mao Jie and verify the truth on both sides.

sentences.zh: 今聖恩不忍致之於理，更使曲直之分不明。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty's gracious kindness, unwilling to put him through the law, only makes right and wrong harder to distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty's gracious reluctance to bring the case to law only makes right and wrong harder to distinguish.

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「所以不考，欲兩全玠及言事者耳。

translations.literal: " Cao said: "The reason I do not investigate is that I wish to preserve both Jie and the informant.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao said, "The reason I do not investigate is that I wish to preserve both Mao Jie and the informant.

sentences.zh: 」洽對曰：「玠信有謗主之言，當肆之市朝；

translations.literal: " He Qia replied: "If Jie truly had words slandering his lord, he ought to be executed in the marketplace;
translations.idiomatic: " He Qia replied, "If Mao Jie truly spoke slander against his lord, he ought to be executed in the public marketplace.

sentences.zh: 若玠無此言，言事者加誣大臣以誤主聽，不加檢覈，臣竊不安。

translations.literal: If Jie had no such words, then the informant added false charges against a high minister to mislead his lord's hearing—if this is not checked and verified, your subject privately feels uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: If Mao Jie said no such thing, then the informant has falsely accused a high minister and misled his lord's judgment. If that is not investigated, your subject cannot rest easy.

sentences.zh: 」操卒不窮治，玠遂免黜，終於家。

translations.literal: " Cao in the end did not pursue the matter thoroughly; Jie was then dismissed from office and lived out his days at home.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao in the end did not pursue the matter to the end. Mao Jie was dismissed from office and lived out his days at home.

sentences.zh: 是時西曹掾沛國丁儀用事，玠之獲罪，儀有力焉；

translations.literal: At this time Ding Yi of Pei, Western Bureau Aide, was in power; in Jie's conviction Yi had force behind it;
translations.idiomatic: At this time Ding Yi of Pei, Western Bureau Aide, held power, and he had been instrumental in Mao Jie's conviction.

sentences.zh: 群下畏之側目。

translations.literal: The subordinates feared him and looked askance.
translations.idiomatic: The officials feared him and watched him with sidelong glances.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射何夔及東曹屬東莞徐弈獨不事儀，儀譖弈，出為魏郡太守，賴桓階左右之得免。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing He Kui and Eastern Bureau Subordinate Xu Yi of Dongguan alone would not serve Yi; Yi slandered Yi, who was sent out as Administrator of Wei Commandery; thanks to Huan Jie's support on both sides he escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing He Kui and Eastern Bureau Subordinate Xu Yi of Dongguan alone refused to court Ding Yi. Ding Yi slandered Xu Yi, who was sent out as Administrator of Wei Commandery, but thanks to Huan Jie's intervention on both sides he escaped further punishment.

sentences.zh: 尚書傅選謂何夔曰：「儀已害毛玠，子宜少下之。

translations.literal: Master of Writing Fu Xuan said to He Kui: "Yi has already harmed Mao Jie—you ought to defer to him a little.
translations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Fu Xuan said to He Kui, "Ding Yi has already brought down Mao Jie—you ought to defer to him a little.

sentences.zh: 」夔曰：「為不義，適足害其身，焉能害人！

translations.literal: " Kui said: "To do wrong merely suffices to harm oneself—how can one harm others!
translations.idiomatic: " He Kui said, "To do wrong is enough to destroy oneself—how can it destroy others!

sentences.zh: 且懷奸佞之心，立於明朝，其得久乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, to harbor a treacherous and fawning heart and stand in a bright court—can that last long!
translations.idiomatic: And to harbor a treacherous heart while standing in an enlightened court—can that last long!

sentences.zh: 」崔琰從弟林，嘗與陳群共論冀州人士，稱琰為首，群以智不存身貶之。

translations.literal: " Cui Yan's younger cousin from the father's side, Lin, once discussed men of Ji Province with Chen Qun; he praised Yan as foremost, and Qun belittled him on the ground that his wisdom did not preserve his person.
translations.idiomatic: " Cui Lin, a younger cousin of Cui Yan on his father's side, once discussed the leading men of Ji Province with Chen Qun. Lin ranked Cui Yan first; Qun belittled him on the ground that his wisdom had not preserved his life.

sentences.zh: 林曰：「大丈夫為有邂逅耳，即如卿諸人，良足貴乎□」

translations.literal: Lin said: "A great man acts when there is encounter—that is all; as for people like you, are they really worth valuing?"
translations.idiomatic: Lin said, "A great man acts when the moment calls—that is all. As for men like you, are you really worth so much?"

sentences.zh: 五月，己亥朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Fifth month, first day of the cycle yihai, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the first day of the cycle yihai, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 代郡烏桓三大人皆稱單于，恃力驕恣，太守不能治。

translations.literal: The three Wuhuan chieftains of Dai Commandery all called themselves Chanyu; relying on their strength they were arrogant and willful, and the Administrator could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Three Wuhuan chieftains in Dai Commandery all styled themselves Chanyu. Trusting in their strength, they were arrogant and unruly, and the Administrator could not control them.

sentences.zh: 魏王操以丞相倉曹屬裴潛為太守，欲授以精兵。

translations.literal: King Cao of Wei appointed Pei Qian of the Chancellor's Treasury Bureau, Attendant Officer, as Administrator, and wished to grant him elite troops.
translations.idiomatic: King Cao appointed Pei Qian, Attendant Officer in the Chancellor's Treasury Bureau, Administrator of the commandery, and wished to give him elite troops.

sentences.zh: 潛曰：「單于自知放橫日久，今多將兵往，必懼而拒境，少將則不見憚，宜以計謀圖之。

translations.literal: Qian said: "The Chanyu knows himself to have been willful for a long time; if many troops are sent now, he will surely fear it and bar the border; if few are sent he will not regard it with respect—it is fitting to take him by strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Qian said, "The Chanyu knows he has been lawless for a long time. If I go with many troops, he will surely fear it and close the border. If I go with few, he will not respect me. The thing to do is take him by strategy.

sentences.zh: 」遂單車之郡，單于驚喜。

translations.literal: " He then went to the commandery alone in a single carriage; the Chanyu was surprised and delighted.
translations.idiomatic: " He then went to the commandery alone in a single carriage. The Chanyu was surprised and delighted.

sentences.zh: 潛撫以恩威，單于讋服。

translations.literal: Qian soothed him with kindness and authority; the Chanyu submitted in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Qian won him over with kindness and authority, and the Chanyu submitted in awe.

sentences.zh: 初，南匈奴久居塞內，與編戶大同而不輸貢賦。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Southern Xiongnu had long dwelt within the passes, the same as registered households yet paying no tribute or levies.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Southern Xiongnu had long lived within the frontier passes, treated the same as registered households yet paying no tribute or levies.

sentences.zh: 議者恐其戶口滋蔓，浸難禁制，宜豫為之防。

translations.literal: Those in counsel feared their population would spread and grow, gradually becoming hard to restrain; it was fitting to guard against this in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Counselors feared their population would spread and grow until they became hard to control, and argued that precautions should be taken in advance.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，南單于呼廚泉入朝於魏，魏王操因留之於鄴，使右賢王去卑監其國。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, the Southern Chanyu Huchuquan came to court at Wei; King Cao of Wei thereupon detained him at Ye and sent the Right Worthy King Qubie to oversee the nation.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, the Southern Chanyu Huchuquan came to court at Wei. King Cao detained him at Ye and sent the Right Worthy King Qubie to oversee the Xiongnu lands.

sentences.zh: 單于歲給綿、絹、錢、穀如列侯，子孫傳襲其號。

translations.literal: The Chanyu was given silk floss, fine silk, money, and grain each year like a full marquis; sons and grandsons inherited the title in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu received each year silk floss, fine silk, money, and grain like a full marquis, and the title passed in succession to his sons and grandsons.

sentences.zh: 分其眾為五部，各立其貴人為帥，選漢人為司馬以監督之。

translations.literal: His multitude was divided into five divisions; in each a noble was established as commander; Han Chinese were selected as Sima to supervise them.
translations.idiomatic: His people were divided into five divisions, each under one of their nobles as commander, with Han Chinese selected as Sima to supervise them.

sentences.zh: 八月，魏以大理鐘繇為相國。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Wei appointed Zhong Yao, Director of Justice, as Chancellor of State.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Wei appointed Zhong Yao, Director of Justice, Chancellor of State.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，魏王操治兵擊孫權；

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, King Cao of Wei marshaled troops and attacked Sun Quan;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, King Cao marshaled his troops and attacked Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，至譙。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, he reached Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he reached Qiao.
